title.raw: 卷一百七十四 列傳第一百二十四: 李德裕 Volume 174, Biography 124: Li Deyu

sentences.zh: 李德裕李德裕，字文饒，趙郡人。

translations.literal: Li Deyu, Li Deyu — style name Wenrao, a native of Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu, style name Wenrao, was a native of Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖棲筠，御史大夫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qi Yun was Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Pei Qiyun served as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 父吉甫，趙國忠公，元和初宰相。

translations.literal: His father Jifu was Duke Zhong of Zhao, a chief minister in the early Yuanhe era.
translations.idiomatic: His father Li Jifu, Duke Zhong of Zhao, had been chancellor at the start of the Yuanhe reign.

sentences.zh: 祖、父自有傳。

translations.literal: Separate biographies exist for grandfather and father.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather and father have their own biographies.

sentences.zh: 德裕幼有壯誌，苦心力學，尤精《西漢書》、《左氏春秋》。

translations.literal: From youth Deyu had a bold will; he studied with bitter effort and was especially expert in the Book of Han and Zuo's Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was ambitious, studied with intense dedication, and became especially adept in the Book of Han and the Zuo Tradition.

sentences.zh: 恥與諸生同鄉賦，不喜科試。

translations.literal: He was ashamed to join other students in the district tribute exam and disliked the civil-service examinations.
translations.idiomatic: He would not sit the district tribute exam alongside ordinary students and had no taste for the formal examination track.

sentences.zh: 年才及冠，誌業大成。

translations.literal: Before he had reached twenty, his learning and purpose were already complete.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he came of age, his studies and ambition were already fully formed.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，以父譴逐蠻方，隨侍左右，不求仕進。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyuan era, because his father was banished to the southern frontier, he attended at his side and sought no advancement.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenyuan period, when his father was exiled to the far south, he stayed at his father's side and sought no office.

sentences.zh: 元和初，以父再秉國鈞，避嫌不仕臺省，累辟諸府從事。

translations.literal: At the start of Yuanhe, when his father again held the national helm, he avoided office in the central ministries out of conflict-of-interest scruples, and was repeatedly invited to serve as staff in various prefectural offices.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanhe began and his father again headed the government, he declined central posts to avoid suspicion and accepted a series of staff appointments in regional administrations.

sentences.zh: 十一年，張弘靖罷相，鎮太原，辟為掌書記。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Zhang Hongjing left the chancellorship and took charge at Taiyuan; he recruited Deyu as chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In 816 Zhang Hongjing left the chancellorship to govern Taiyuan and appointed him chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 由大理評事得殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: From the post of reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review he obtained the post of Attending Censor within the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from judicial reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review to Attending Censor within the Palace.

sentences.zh: 十四年府罷，從弘靖入朝，真拜監察御史。

translations.literal: When the office was dissolved in the fourteenth year, he followed Hongjing to court and was formally appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongjing's term ended in 819, he accompanied him to the capital and received formal appointment as Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，穆宗即位，召入翰林，充學士。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year Muzong succeeded; Deyu was summoned to the Hanlin Academy as academician.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when Muzong ascended in the first month, he was summoned to the Hanlin Academy as an academician.

sentences.zh: 帝在東宮，素聞吉甫之名，既見德裕，尤重之。

translations.literal: The emperor, while still crown prince, had long heard of Jifu's reputation; once he met Deyu he valued him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: While still heir apparent the emperor had long known Li Jifu's name; meeting Deyu, he esteemed him even more highly.

sentences.zh: 禁中書詔大手筆，多詔德裕草之。

translations.literal: For important edicts and drafts within the palace, the emperor often ordered Deyu to compose them.
translations.idiomatic: Major palace edicts and memorial drafts were often entrusted to Deyu to write.

sentences.zh: 是月，召對思政殿，賜金紫之服。

translations.literal: That same month he was summoned for audience at the Hall of Reflection on Governance and granted the gold-and-purple court robes.
translations.idiomatic: That month he was received in audience at the Hall of Reflection on Governance and awarded gold-and-purple insignia.

sentences.zh: 逾月，改屯田員外郎。

translations.literal: After more than a month he was transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue's Field Section.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he was moved to vice director in the Ministry of Revenue's field administration.

sentences.zh: 穆宗不持政道，多所恩貸，戚裏諸親，邪謀請謁；

translations.literal: Muzong did not uphold proper governance; he granted many favors, and relatives of the empress clan and others plotted improper requests;
translations.idiomatic: Muzong did not maintain disciplined government. He bestowed favors widely; empress-clan kin and others pressed improper access through intrigue;

sentences.zh: 傳導中人之旨，與權臣往來，德裕嫉之。

translations.literal: they conveyed the eunuchs' wishes and associated with power-holders; Deyu resented this.
translations.idiomatic: they relayed the eunuchs' will and trafficked with powerful ministers—conduct Deyu deeply resented.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年正月，上疏論之曰：「伏見國朝故事，駙馬緣是親密，不合與朝廷要官往來。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Changqing, he submitted a memorial stating: "I observe that in our dynasty's precedents, imperial sons-in-law, being intimate kin, should not associate with important officials of the court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Changqing 1 (821) he memorialized: "I observe our dynasty's precedent that sons-in-law of the throne, as intimate kin, should not visit senior court officials privately.

sentences.zh: 玄宗開元中，禁止尤切。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xuanzong's Kaiyuan reign the prohibition was especially strict.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanzong in the Kaiyuan era the ban was especially strict.

sentences.zh: 訪聞近日駙馬輒至宰相及要官私第，此輩無他才伎可以延接，唯是泄漏禁密；

translations.literal: I have heard that recently sons-in-law have repeatedly gone to the private residences of chancellors and key officials; these men have no other talent to discuss with them but only leak forbidden secrets;
translations.idiomatic: I have learned that recently imperial sons-in-law have gone repeatedly to chancellors' and key officials' private homes. They have no real conversation to offer—only the leaking of palace secrets;

sentences.zh: 交通中外，群情所知，以為甚弊。

translations.literal: traffic with inside and outside is known to all; the sentiment is that this is a great abuse.
translations.idiomatic: their contact with court insiders and outsiders is widely known and regarded as a grave abuse.

sentences.zh: 其朝官素是雜流，則不妨來往。

translations.literal: If a court officer is of mixed rank by origin, his coming and going may be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: If the official in question is of lesser or mixed rank, the visits may be allowed.

sentences.zh: 若職在清列，豈可知聞？

translations.literal: If his office is in the clean ranks, how can he be known and heard of in such traffic?
translations.idiomatic: But if he holds a post in the elite ranks, how can he permit such associations?

sentences.zh: 伏乞宣示宰臣，其駙馬諸親，今後公事即於中書見宰相，請不令詣私第。」

translations.literal: I beg that Your Majesty instruct the chancellors: henceforth sons-in-law and their kin, for public business, should see the chancellor at the Secretariat and should not be allowed to go to private residences."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Your Majesty instruct the chancellors that henceforth sons-in-law and their kin should meet chancellors only at the Secretariat on public business and not be allowed at private residences."

sentences.zh: 上然之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 尋轉考功郎中、知制誥。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Personnel's examination section and given charge of drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made director of examinations in the Ministry of Personnel and entrusted with drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，轉中書舍人，學士如故。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year, he was transferred to Secretariat Drafter while retaining his academician status.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of 822 he became Secretariat Drafter while remaining a Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 初，吉甫在相位時，牛僧孺、李宗閔應制舉直言極諫科。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jifu was chancellor, Niu Sengru and Li Zongmin had entered the special examination on forthright criticism and utmost remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Jifu was chancellor, Niu Sengru and Li Zongmin had taken the special examination on forthright criticism and utmost remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 二人對詔，深詆時政之失，吉甫泣訴於上前。

translations.literal: The two men's answers to the edict deeply denounced failures of the times; Jifu wept and complained before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Their examination answers harshly criticized government failings; Jifu wept and lodged complaint before the throne.

sentences.zh: 由是，考策官皆貶，事在《李宗閔傳》。

translations.literal: Thereupon all the examiners were demoted; the matter is in the biography of Li Zongmin.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the examiners were all demoted—the account is in Li Zongmin's biography.

sentences.zh: 元和初，用兵伐叛，始於杜黃裳誅蜀。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe, campaigns against rebels began with Du Huangshang's suppression of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yuanhe military campaigns against rebels began with Du Huangshang's pacification of Shu.

sentences.zh: 吉甫經畫，欲定兩河，方欲出師而卒。

translations.literal: Jifu planned strategy, intending to settle the two He regions, but just as he was about to launch troops he died.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu had planned strategy to settle the two He provinces but died just as armies were to march.

sentences.zh: 繼之元衡、裴度。

translations.literal: Wu Yuanheng and Pei Du succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yuanheng and Pei Du followed in succession.

sentences.zh: 而韋貫之、李逢吉沮議，深以用兵為非。

translations.literal: But Wei Guanzhi and Li Fengji obstructed counsel and deeply viewed use of troops as wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guanzhi and Li Fengji blocked the policy and strongly opposed military action.

sentences.zh: 而韋、李相次罷相，故逢吉常怒吉甫、裴度。

translations.literal: Wei and Li were dismissed from the chancellorship in turn; therefore Fengji constantly harbored anger toward Jifu and Pei Du.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Li were removed from office in succession, so Fengji nursed lasting resentment toward Jifu and Pei Du.

sentences.zh: 而德裕於元和時，久之不調，而逢吉、僧孺、宗閔以私怨恆排擯之。

translations.literal: Deyu during Yuanhe for a long time received no transfer; Fengji, Sengru, and Zongmin, with private grievances, constantly blocked and pushed him aside.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanhe Deyu long went without advancement; Fengji, Sengru, and Zongmin, nursing private scores, kept blocking and sidelining him.

sentences.zh: 時德裕與李紳、元稹俱在翰林，以學識才名相類，情頗款密。

translations.literal: At that time Deyu, Li Shen, and Yuan Zhen were all in the Hanlin; alike in learning and repute, they were on warm terms.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Deyu, Li Shen, and Yuan Zhen were all in the Hanlin—men of similar learning and fame—and were on affectionate terms.

sentences.zh: 而逢吉之黨深惡之。

translations.literal: But Fengji's faction deeply hated them.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji's faction hated them deeply.

sentences.zh: 其月，罷學士，出為御史中丞。

translations.literal: That month he was dismissed as academician and sent out as Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: That month he was removed as academician and sent out as Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 其元稹自禁中出，拜工部侍郎、平章事。

translations.literal: That same period Yuan Zhen left the inner palace and was appointed Vice Minister of Works and Associate Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: About then Yuan Zhen left the inner palace and was appointed Vice Minister of Works and Associate Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 三月，輩度自太原復輔政。

translations.literal: In the third month Pei Du returned from Taiyuan to assist government again.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Pei Du returned from Taiyuan to serve again as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 是月，李逢吉亦自襄陽入朝，乃密賂纖人，構成於方獄。

translations.literal: That month Li Fengji also entered from Xiangyang; he secretly bribed informers and constructed matters in regional prisons.
translations.idiomatic: That month Li Fengji also entered from Xiangyang; he secretly paid informers and engineered cases in frontier jurisdictions.

sentences.zh: 六月，元稹、裴度俱罷相。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Yuan Zhen and Pei Du were both removed as chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Yuan Zhen and Pei Du were both dismissed from the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 稹出為同州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhen was sent out as governor of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was sent out as governor of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 逢吉代裴度為門下侍郎、平章事。

translations.literal: Fengji replaced Pei Du as Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji replaced Pei Du as Secretariat Vice Director and Associate Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 既得權位，銳意報怨。

translations.literal: Once he held power, he eagerly sought revenge.
translations.idiomatic: Once in power he pressed revenge with sharp intent.

sentences.zh: 時德裕與牛僧孺俱有相望，逢吉欲引僧孺，懼紳與德裕禁中沮之；

translations.literal: At that time both Deyu and Niu Sengru enjoyed standing; Fengji wished to bring Sengru in but feared Li Shen and Deyu would obstruct him in the palace;
translations.idiomatic: Deyu and Niu Sengru both had standing; Fengji wished to elevate Sengru but feared Shen and Deyu in the palace would block him;

sentences.zh: 九月，出德裕為浙西觀察使，尋引僧孺同平章事。

translations.literal: in the ninth month Deyu was sent out as military commissioner of Zhexi; soon Sengru was brought in as associate chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: in the ninth month Deyu was posted as Zhexi observation commissioner; soon Sengru was brought in as associate chief minister.

sentences.zh: 由是交怨愈深。

translations.literal: From this the mutual enmity grew deeper.
translations.idiomatic: From this mutual hatred only deepened.

sentences.zh: 潤州承王國清兵亂之後，前使竇易直傾府藏賞給，軍旋浸驕，財用殫竭。

translations.literal: Run prefecture, after Wang Guoqing's mutiny, had seen the previous commissioner Dou Yizhi empty the treasury in rewards; when the army returned it grew increasingly arrogant and resources were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Runzhou, after Wang Guoqing's rebellion, had seen the prior commissioner Dou Yizhi drain the treasury in rewards; on return the troops grew arrogant and funds ran dry.

sentences.zh: 德裕儉於自奉，留州所得，盡以贍軍，雖施與不豐，將卒無怨。

translations.literal: Deyu was frugal in personal upkeep; whatever the prefecture yielded he gave entirely to the army; though his gifts were not lavish, officers and soldiers had no complaint.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu was austere in personal spending and devoted the prefecture's receipts entirely to the troops; though distributions were not lavish, none in the ranks resented him.

sentences.zh: 二年之後，賦輿復集。

translations.literal: After two years, taxes and transport revenues were again collected.
translations.idiomatic: Within two years tax income and transport revenues were restored.

sentences.zh: 德裕壯年得位，銳於布政，凡舊俗之害民者，悉革其弊。

translations.literal: Deyu gained office in his prime and was keen to administer; every old custom harmful to the people he abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the strength of youth he took office eager to govern; every local abuse harming the people he abolished.

sentences.zh: 江、嶺之間信巫祝，惑鬼怪，有父母兄弟厲疾者，舉室棄之而去。

translations.literal: Between the Yangzi and Ling regions people trusted shamans and were deluded by ghosts; when parents, brothers, or kin had severe illness, the whole household abandoned them and left.
translations.idiomatic: Between Yangzi and Nanling people trusted shamans and feared specters; families would abandon kin stricken with serious illness and flee.

sentences.zh: 德裕欲變其風，擇鄉人之有識者，諭之以言，繩之以法，數年之間，弊風頓革。

translations.literal: Deyu wished to change this custom; he chose knowledgeable locals, instructed them in words and bound them by law; within several years the evil practice was suddenly reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu sought to change the custom: he chose knowledgeable locals, instructed and restrained them by law, and within years the vicious practice collapsed.

sentences.zh: 屬郡祠廟，按方誌，前代名臣賢後則祠之。

translations.literal: For prefectural temples he followed local gazetteers: former worthy ministers and worthy descendants were enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: For district shrines he followed gazetteers, enshrining former worthy ministers and worthy descendants.

sentences.zh: 四郡之內，除淫祠一千一十所。

translations.literal: Within four prefectures he abolished licentious shrines numbering 1,110.
translations.idiomatic: Across four prefectures he abolished illicit shrines—1,110 in all.

sentences.zh: 又罷私邑山房一千四百六十，以清寇盜。

translations.literal: He also shut 1,460 private mountain lodges in local communities to suppress banditry.
translations.idiomatic: He also abolished 1,460 private hill lodges in local communities to suppress banditry.

sentences.zh: 人樂其政，優詔嘉之。

translations.literal: The people rejoiced in his governance; an edict of praise commended him.
translations.idiomatic: The people welcomed his rule; the court issued a commendatory edict praising him.

sentences.zh: 昭湣皇帝童年纘歷，頗事奢靡。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaomin succeeded young and was much given to luxury.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jingzong came to the throne young and was much given to extravagance.

sentences.zh: 即位之年七月，詔浙西造銀盝子妝具二十事進內。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of his accession year an edict ordered Zhexi to manufacture twenty sets of silver toilet furnishings for presentation to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of his accession year an edict ordered Zhexi to present twenty silver toilet sets to the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 德裕奏曰：

translations.literal: Deyu memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Deyu submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 時準赦不許進獻。

translations.literal: At that time a recent amnesty forbade presentations.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a recent amnesty forbade such presentations.

sentences.zh: 逾月之後，征貢之使，道路相繼。

translations.literal: After more than a month, envoys seeking tribute followed one another on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: A month later, tribute envoys crowded the roads in succession.

sentences.zh: 故德裕因訴而諷之。

translations.literal: Therefore Deyu, in his complaint, employed indirect criticism.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Deyu used his petition to remonstrate indirectly.

sentences.zh: 事奏，不報。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted but received no answer.

sentences.zh: 又詔進可幅盤條繚綾一千匹，德裕又論曰：

translations.literal: Another edict ordered presentation of 1,000 bolts of patterned silk of set width for trays; Deyu argued again, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Another edict ordered 1,000 bolts of tray-width patterned silk; Deyu argued again:

sentences.zh: 優詔報之。

translations.literal: A commendatory edict replied to him.
translations.idiomatic: The throne replied with a gracious edict.

sentences.zh: 其繚綾罷進。

translations.literal: The silk presentation was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The silk tribute was halted.

sentences.zh: 元和已來，累敕天下州府，不得私度僧尼。

translations.literal: Since Yuanhe, repeated edicts had forbidden prefectures and circuits from ordaining monks and nuns privately.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yuanhe repeated edicts had forbidden prefectures and circuits from ordaining clergy privately.

sentences.zh: 徐州節度使王智興聚貨無厭，以敬宗誕月，請於泗州置僧壇，度人資福，以邀厚利。

translations.literal: Xuzhou military commissioner Wang Zhixing, insatiable in amassing goods, on Jingzong's birthday month asked to set up an ordination altar at Sizhou to ordain people for merit and reap heavy profit.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhixing, Xuzhou commissioner, insatiable for profit, on Jingzong's birthday month asked to establish an ordination altar at Sizhou to ordain the faithful for merit—and heavy fees.

sentences.zh: 江、淮之民，皆群黨渡淮。

translations.literal: People of Jiang and Huai all crossed the Huai in groups.
translations.idiomatic: People of the Jiang-Huai region crossed the Huai in crowds.

sentences.zh: 德裕奏論曰：

translations.literal: Deyu submitted argument, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Deyu submitted argument saying:

sentences.zh: 狀奏，即日詔徐州罷之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, that very day an edict ordered Xuzhou to stop.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was in, that very day an edict ordered Xuzhou to cease.

sentences.zh: 敬宗荒僻日甚，遊幸無恆；

translations.literal: Jingzong grew daily more dissolute; his tours had no constancy;
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong grew daily more dissolute in conduct; his tours had no fixed pattern;

sentences.zh: 疏遠賢能，昵比群小。

translations.literal: he kept distance from the worthy and drew near petty men.
translations.idiomatic: he distanced worthy men and drew near petty favorites.

sentences.zh: 坐朝月不二三度，大臣罕得進言。

translations.literal: He held court two or three times a month at most; great ministers rarely gained speech.
translations.idiomatic: He sat court at most two or three times a month; great ministers rarely gained audience to speak.

sentences.zh: 海內憂危，慮移宗社。

translations.literal: Within the realm there was alarm; some feared the dynasty might shift.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was alarmed; some feared the throne itself might shift.

sentences.zh: 德裕身居廉鎮，傾心王室，遣使獻《丹扆箴》六首，曰：

translations.literal: Though Deyu held a frontier post, he turned his heart to the royal house and sent envoys presenting six Admonitions for the Crimson Screen, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Deyu, though on the frontier, turned his heart to the throne and sent envoys presenting six "Admonitions for the Crimson Screen," saying:

sentences.zh: 其《宵衣箴》曰：「先王聽政，昧爽以俟。

translations.literal: The Admonition on Early Rising says: "Former kings heard governance; at first light they waited.
translations.idiomatic: The Early Rising admonition: "Former kings attended to government, waiting from first light.

sentences.zh: 雞鳴既盈，日出而視。

translations.literal: When the cock's crow had filled, at sunrise they looked forth.
translations.idiomatic: When the cocks had crowed full, at sunrise they looked forth.

sentences.zh: 伯禹大聖，寸陰為貴。

translations.literal: Lord Yu the Great Sage held each inch of shadow precious.
translations.idiomatic: Yu the Great Sage treasured every inch of shadow.

sentences.zh: 光武至仁，反支不忌。

translations.literal: Guangwu the most benevolent did not fear the negative branch day.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu the most benevolent did not shun the "negative branch" day for rest.

sentences.zh: 無俾姜後，獨去簪珥。

translations.literal: Do not let the Empress Jiang go alone removing hairpins and earrings.
translations.idiomatic: Do not let an empress like Jiang go alone removing hairpins and earrings.

sentences.zh: 彤管記言，克念前誌。」

translations.literal: The red tube records words; hold fast to former aims."
translations.idiomatic: The red tube records words—hold fast to the lessons of the past."

sentences.zh: 其《正服箴》曰：「聖人作服，法象可觀。

translations.literal: The Admonition on Proper Dress says: "The sage made garments; their emblems can be seen.
translations.idiomatic: The Proper Dress admonition: "The sage fashioned dress with emblems one may read.

sentences.zh: 雖在宴遊，尚不懷安。

translations.literal: Even in banquets and excursions, one does not dwell in ease.
translations.idiomatic: Even at feast or hunt one does not sink into comfort.

sentences.zh: 汲黯莊色，能正不冠。

translations.literal: Ji An with stern countenance could correct one not wearing the cap.
translations.idiomatic: Ji An with stern bearing could correct one who wore no cap.

sentences.zh: 楊阜毅然，亦譏縹紈。

translations.literal: Yang Fu resolutely also rebuked pale silk finery.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu with equal sternness rebuked pale silk finery.

sentences.zh: 四時所禦，各有其官。

translations.literal: What each of the four seasons commands has its proper office.
translations.idiomatic: Each season's proper attire has its proper office.

sentences.zh: 非此勿服，惟辟所難。」

translations.literal: Without this, do not wear it—the sovereign alone is hard pressed."
translations.idiomatic: Wear no other—the ruler alone may be pressed."

sentences.zh: 其《罷獻箴》曰：「漢文罷獻，詔還騄耳。

translations.literal: The Admonition on Ceasing Tribute says: "Han Wen abolished tribute; an edict returned the dappled horses.
translations.idiomatic: The Ceasing Tribute admonition: "Emperor Wen of Han ended tribute; edict returned the dappled horses.

sentences.zh: 鑾輅徐驅，焉用千里？

translations.literal: The imperial carriage drives slowly—what need of a thousand li?
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage moves slowly—what need of horses for a thousand li?

sentences.zh: 厥後令王，亦能恭己。

translations.literal: Later worthy kings also could restrain themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Later worthy kings likewise could restrain themselves.

sentences.zh: 翟裘既焚，筒布則毀。

translations.literal: Once the sable cloak was burnt, bamboo-cloth sheets were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Once the marten cloak was burned, bamboo-cloth sheets were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 道德為麗，慈仁為美。

translations.literal: Virtue as adornment, kindness and benevolence as beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue as ornament, kindness and benevolence as beauty.

sentences.zh: 不過天道，斯為至理。」

translations.literal: Not to exceed Heaven's Way—this is the utmost principle."
translations.idiomatic: Not to overstep Heaven's way—that is the highest principle."

sentences.zh: 其《納誨箴》曰：「惟後納誨，以求厥中。

translations.literal: The Admonition on Receiving Remonstrance says: "Only when the ruler receives remonstrance can the mean be sought.
translations.idiomatic: The Receiving Remonstrance admonition: "Only when the sovereign heeds counsel can the middle way be found.

sentences.zh: 從善如流，乃能成功。

translations.literal: Following good as flowing water—only then can success be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Heeding good counsel as water flows downhill—only then can success be won.

sentences.zh: 漢驁流湎，舉白浮鐘。

translations.literal: Han Ai dissipated in wine, raising cups with floating bells.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ai of Han drowned in wine, raising cups while bells floated.

sentences.zh: 魏睿侈汰，淩霄作宮。

translations.literal: Wei Rui was extravagant and wasteful, building a palace to pierce the sky.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Rui of Wei was prodigal, erecting a Lingxiao Palace that scraped the heavens.

sentences.zh: 忠雖不忤，善亦不從。

translations.literal: Though loyalty did not offend, goodness was still not followed.
translations.idiomatic: Though loyal words gave no offense, good counsel was still not heeded.

sentences.zh: 以規為瑱，是謂塞聰。」

translations.literal: Taking admonition as earplugs—this is called stopping up the ears."
translations.idiomatic: Treating remonstrance as ear-stoppers—this is what it means to deafen oneself."

sentences.zh: 其《辯邪箴》曰：「居上處深，在察微萌。

translations.literal: The Admonition on Discerning Evil says: "Dwelling high and sitting deep—in contemplating the slightest sprouting.
translations.idiomatic: The Discerning Evil admonition: "Sitting high and looking deep—to detect evil in its first sprouting.

sentences.zh: 雖有讒慝，不能蔽明。

translations.literal: Though there are slanderers and villains, they cannot obscure brightness.
translations.idiomatic: Though slanderers and schemers exist, they cannot hide the light.

sentences.zh: 漢之有昭，德過周成。

translations.literal: In Han there was Zhao—virtue surpassing Zhou Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han there was Emperor Zhao, whose virtue exceeded King Cheng of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 上書知偽，照奸得情。

translations.literal: On memorials knowing forgery, shining on treachery and obtaining the facts.
translations.idiomatic: He knew forged memorials for what they were and exposed treachery to the truth.

sentences.zh: 燕、蓋既折，王猷洽平。

translations.literal: With Yan and Gai already broken, the king's plans flowed smoothly.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Yan and Gai factions were crushed, the royal enterprise ran smooth.

sentences.zh: 百代之後，乃流淑聲。」

translations.literal: A hundred generations later, a fine reputation still flows forth."
translations.idiomatic: A hundred generations on, his fair name still resounds."

sentences.zh: 其《防微箴》曰：「天子之孝，敬遵王度。

translations.literal: The Admonition on Guarding the Slight says: "The Son of Heaven's filial piety—reverently following royal measures.
translations.idiomatic: The Guarding the Slight admonition: "The Son of Heaven's filial piety lies in reverently keeping royal rule.

sentences.zh: 安必思危，乃無遺慮。

translations.literal: In safety one must think of danger—then no concerns are left behind.
translations.idiomatic: In peace one must think of peril—then no worry is left unattended.

sentences.zh: 亂臣猖蹶，非可遽數。

translations.literal: Rebellious ministers rampage wildly—not to be counted in haste.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellious ministers run riot—they cannot be numbered offhand.

sentences.zh: 玄黃莫辨，觸瑟始仆。

translations.literal: Black and yellow indistinguishable—only when touching the zither did he fall.
translations.idiomatic: When black and yellow could not be told apart, it took a snapped zither-string to bring him down.

sentences.zh: 柏谷微行，豺豕塞路。

translations.literal: A secret journey through Bailu Valley—wolves and pigs blocked the road.
translations.idiomatic: An incognito tour through Bailu Valley found wolves and swine blocking the way.

sentences.zh: 睹貌獻飧，斯可誡懼。」

translations.literal: Seeing his countenance, one offered food—this can warn and inspire fear."
translations.idiomatic: A stranger saw his face and offered a meal—such is the lesson that should inspire dread."

sentences.zh: 帝手詔答曰：「卿文雅大臣，方隅重寄。

translations.literal: The emperor answered by hand edict: "You are a cultured great minister, with heavy trust in a frontier region.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied in his own hand: "You are a cultivated senior minister, entrusted with weighty charge in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 表率諸部，肅清全吳。

translations.literal: Setting the example for all districts, bringing order to all Wu.
translations.idiomatic: You set the standard for every commandery and brought peace to all Wu.

sentences.zh: 化洽行春，風澄坐嘯，眷言善政，想嘆在懷。

translations.literal: Your transforming influence spread in spring governance; your wind was clear as you sat and governed at ease—when I think on your good policies, admiration fills my breast.
translations.idiomatic: Your rule harmonized the land like spring itself; your governance was serene—and when I recall your good policies, admiration wells up in me.

sentences.zh: 卿之宗門，累著聲績，冠內廷者兩代，襲侯伯者六朝。

translations.literal: Your clan for generations has shown illustrious achievement—two generations topped the inner court, six dynasties in succession held marquisates and earldoms.
translations.idiomatic: Your house has piled up renown for generations—two generations led the inner court, six in a row inherited marquisates and earldoms.

sentences.zh: 果能激愛君之誠，喻詩人之旨。

translations.literal: Truly you could stir the sincerity of loving the lord and illustrate the poet's intent.
translations.idiomatic: You have truly roused a loyal heart and embodied the poets' intent.

sentences.zh: 在遠而不忘忠告，諷上而常深慮微。

translations.literal: Though far away, you do not forget faithful counsel; admonishing above, you always think deeply of guarding the slight.
translations.idiomatic: Though distant, you do not forget faithful remonstrance; in admonishing your sovereign, you ever dwell on nipping peril in the bud.

sentences.zh: 博我以端躬，約予以循禮。

translations.literal: You broadened me with upright conduct and bound me to follow ritual.
translations.idiomatic: You enlarged my mind with upright example and constrained me within ritual.

sentences.zh: 三復規諫，累夕稱嗟。

translations.literal: Three times I reviewed your admonitions and praised them night after night.
translations.idiomatic: I read your admonitions again and again and praised them night after night.

sentences.zh: 置之座隅，用比韋弘之益；

translations.literal: I placed them at the corner of my seat, to compare with Wei Hong's benefit;
translations.idiomatic: I keep them beside my seat, as one might Wei Hong's counsel;

sentences.zh: 銘諸心腑，何啻藥石之功？

translations.literal: inscribed them on the heart's core—how is that less than medicine-stone's effect?
translations.idiomatic: I inscribe them on my heart—what is that but the force of healing stone and medicine?

sentences.zh: 卿既以投誠，朕每懷開諫，茍有過舉，無忘密陳。

translations.literal: Since you have offered sincerity, I always welcome open remonstrance; if there be any error on my part, do not forget to report it in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Now that you have shown such sincerity, I ever welcome frank counsel; should I err, do not fail to tell me in confidence.

sentences.zh: 山川既遐，睠屬何已，必當克己，以副乃誠。」

translations.literal: Mountains and rivers are far—how could my regard ever end? You must restrain yourself to fulfill this sincerity."
translations.idiomatic: Though mountains and rivers lie between us, my regard for you does not cease; you must discipline yourself to match this sincerity."

sentences.zh: 德裕意在切諫，不欲斥言，托箴以盡意。

translations.literal: Deyu's intent was earnest admonition; not wishing to speak bluntly, he relied on admonitions to express his meaning fully.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu meant to admonish earnestly; unwilling to speak plainly, he used these admonitions to say all he meant.

sentences.zh: 《宵衣》，諷坐朝稀晚也；

translations.literal: Early Rising satirizes holding court late and seldom;
translations.idiomatic: Early Rising rebukes infrequent and tardy audiences;

sentences.zh: 《正服》，諷服禦乖異也；

translations.literal: Correct Dress satirizes irregularities in imperial dress;
translations.idiomatic: Correct Dress rebukes irregular court attire;

sentences.zh: 《罷獻》，諷征求玩好也；

translations.literal: Ceasing Tribute satirizes levying curios and delights;
translations.idiomatic: Ceasing Tribute rebukes exactions of curios and luxuries;

sentences.zh: 《納誨》，諷侮棄讜言也；

translations.literal: Receiving Remonstrance satirizes contempt for forthright counsel;
translations.idiomatic: Receiving Remonstrance rebukes scorning honest counsel;

sentences.zh: 《辨邪》，諷信任群小也；

translations.literal: Discerning Evil satirizes trusting petty men;
translations.idiomatic: Discerning Evil rebukes trusting petty men;

sentences.zh: 《防微》，諷輕出遊幸也。

translations.literal: Guarding the Slight satirizes going out on tour too lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Guarding the Slight rebukes rash excursions from the palace.

sentences.zh: 帝雖不能盡用其言，命學士韋處厚殷勤答詔，頗嘉納其心焉。

translations.literal: Though the emperor could not fully use his words, he ordered Academician Wei Chuhou to answer the edict earnestly and quite appreciated his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor could not adopt all he said, he had Academician Wei Chuhou draft a warm reply and clearly valued his intent.

sentences.zh: 德裕久留江介，心戀闕廷，因事寄情，望回聖獎。

translations.literal: Deyu had long remained in the Jiang region, his heart longing for the court; through the affair he sent feeling, hoping for imperial reward.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu had long stayed in the lower Yangtze, yearning for the capital; in this matter he poured out his heart, hoping for favor from the throne.

sentences.zh: 而逢吉當軸，枳棘其塗，竟不得內徙。

translations.literal: But Fengji held the axis of power, brambles blocking his path—ultimately he could not be moved inward.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Li Fengji held the helm, and thorns choked his road—he never won transfer back to court.

sentences.zh: 寶歷二年，亳州言出聖水，飲之者愈疾。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoli, Bozhou reported that holy water had appeared; those who drank it were cured of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoli year 2, Bozhou reported holy water whose drinkers were healed of disease.

sentences.zh: 德裕奏曰：「臣訪聞此水，本因妖僧誑惑，狡計丐錢。

translations.literal: Deyu memorialized: "In my inquiries I learned that this water arose from a deceitful monk's delusion and a cunning scheme to beg money.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu submitted: "My inquiries show this water began with a rogue monk's deceit and a cunning scheme to extort money.

sentences.zh: 數月已來，江南之人，奔走塞路。

translations.literal: For months now, people south of the Yangtze have clogged the roads in their rush.
translations.idiomatic: For months, people south of the Yangtze have jammed the roads in their rush.

sentences.zh: 每三二十家，都顧一人取水。

translations.literal: Every twenty or thirty households together hired one man to fetch water.
translations.idiomatic: Every twenty or thirty households together hired one man to fetch the water.

sentences.zh: 擬取之時，疾者斷食葷血，既飲之後，又二七日蔬飧，危疾之人，俟之愈病。

translations.literal: When they were about to fetch it, the sick abstained from meat and blood; after drinking, they ate only vegetables for another fourteen days, while those gravely ill waited for recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Before fetching it, the sick gave up meat and blood; after drinking, they ate only plain fare for fourteen days more, and the critically ill waited to see if they improved.

sentences.zh: 其水鬥價三貫，而取者益之他水，沿路轉以市人，老疾飲之，多至危篤。

translations.literal: The water sold for three strings per dou, yet fetchers mixed in other water and peddled it along the road; the old and sick who drank it often fell into grave danger.
translations.idiomatic: A dou of the water cost three strings of cash, yet fetchers adulterated it with other water and resold it along the road; the aged and ailing who drank it often grew critically ill.

sentences.zh: 昨點兩浙、福建百姓渡江者，日三五十人。

translations.literal: Yesterday I tallied commoners from the two Zhe circuits and Fujian crossing the river—fifty or so each day.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday I counted commoners from the two Zhe circuits and Fujian crossing the river—thirty to fifty a day.

sentences.zh: 臣於蒜山渡已加捉搦。

translations.literal: At Suanshan Ford I have already added arrests and seizures.
translations.idiomatic: At Suanshan Ford I have already begun seizing them.

sentences.zh: 若不絕其根本，終無益黎氓。

translations.literal: If its root is not cut off, the common people will never benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Unless the root is cut off, the people will never be helped.

sentences.zh: 昔吳時有聖水，宋、齊有聖火，事皆妖妄，古人所非。

translations.literal: In Wu times there was holy water; in Song and Qi there was holy fire—affairs all of sorcery, condemned by the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: In Wu there was holy water; in Song and Qi, holy fire—all sorcery, which the ancients rejected.

sentences.zh: 乞下本道觀察使令狐楚，速令填塞，以絕妖源。」

translations.literal: I beg that the circuit observation commissioner Linghu Chu of this circuit be ordered at once to fill it in and cut off the source of sorcery."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty order the observation commissioner of this circuit, Linghu Chu, to fill it in at once and stop this source of sorcery."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: His request was granted.

sentences.zh: 敬宗為兩街道士趙歸真說以神仙之術，宜訪求異人以師其道。

translations.literal: Jingzong, on the advice of the two-street Daoist Zhao Guizhen, was told of immortal arts and that he should seek out extraordinary men to study the Way under them.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong, urged by the Capital Daoist Zhao Guizhen, was told of immortal arts and advised to seek extraordinary men as teachers of the Way.

sentences.zh: 僧惟貞、齊賢、正簡說以祠禱修福，以致長年。

translations.literal: The monks Weizhen, Qixian, and Zhengjian preached that prayer and sacrifice build merit and lead to long life.
translations.idiomatic: The monks Weizhen, Qixian, and Zhengjian preached that rites and prayer earn merit and bring long life.

sentences.zh: 四人皆出入禁中，日進邪說。

translations.literal: All four came and went within the Forbidden Precinct, daily advancing perverse talk.
translations.idiomatic: All four moved in and out of the inner palace, daily pouring forth perverse counsel.

sentences.zh: 山人杜景先進狀，請於江南求訪異人。

translations.literal: The mountain man Du Jingxian submitted a petition asking that extraordinary men be sought south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: The recluse Du Jingxian submitted a memorial asking that extraordinary men be sought in the south.

sentences.zh: 至浙西，言有隱士周息元，壽數百歲。

translations.literal: Reaching western Zhe, he said there was a recluse, Zhou Xiyuan, who had lived several hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: In western Zhe he named a recluse, Zhou Xiyuan, said to be several hundred years old.

sentences.zh: 帝即令高品、薛季棱往潤州迎之。

translations.literal: The emperor at once ordered Gao Pin and Xue Jiling to go to Runzhou to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately sent Gao Pin and Xue Jiling to Runzhou to escort him.

sentences.zh: 仍詔德裕給公乘遣之。

translations.literal: He also ordered Deyu to supply an official carriage and dispatch him.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Deyu to provide an official carriage and send him on.

sentences.zh: 德裕因中使還，獻疏曰：

translations.literal: Deyu, when the palace envoy returned, submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: When the palace envoy returned, Deyu submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 息元至京，帝館之於山亭，問以道術。

translations.literal: When Xiyuan reached the capital, the emperor lodged him in a mountain pavilion and questioned him on the arts of the Way.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiyuan reached the capital, the emperor housed him in a mountain pavilion and asked him about Daoist arts.

sentences.zh: 自言識張果、葉靜能，詔寫真待詔李士昉問其形狀，圖之以進。

translations.literal: He claimed to know Zhang Guo and Ye Jingneng; the emperor ordered the portrait draftsman Li Shifang to ask their appearance and had pictures drawn and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed acquaintance with Zhang Guo and Ye Jingneng; the emperor ordered the portrait artist Li Shifang to ask their likenesses and had pictures drawn and submitted.

sentences.zh: 息元山野常人，本無道學，言事誕妄，不近人情。

translations.literal: Xiyuan was an ordinary man of mountain wilds, with no learning of the Way at all; his words were absurd and far from human sense.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyuan was a common rustic of the hills, with no true learning of the Way; his talk was absurd and out of touch with reason.

sentences.zh: 及昭湣遇盜而殂，文宗放還江左。

translations.literal: When Zhaomin met assassins and died, Wenzong sent him back to the Jiang southeast.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzong fell to assassins, Wenzong sent him back to the lower Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 德裕深識守正，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Deyu's deep insight and upright guarding of principle were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu's keen judgment and steadfast integrity were all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，就加檢校禮部尚書。

translations.literal: When Wenzong took the throne, Deyu was at once made acting Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: On Wenzong's accession, Deyu was immediately made acting Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 太和三年八月，召為兵部侍郎，裴度薦以為相。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Taihe, he was summoned as Vice Minister of War; Pei Du recommended him for chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Taihe year 3, he was recalled as Vice Minister of War; Pei Du recommended him for the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 而吏部侍郎李宗閔有中人之助，是月拜平章事，懼德裕大用。

translations.literal: But Vice Minister of Personnel Li Zongmin had the eunuchs' help; that same month he was made Grand Counselor, fearing Deyu's great employment.
translations.idiomatic: But Vice Minister of Personnel Li Zongmin had eunuch backing; that month he became Grand Counselor, fearing Deyu would be heavily used.

sentences.zh: 九月，檢校禮部尚書，出為鄭滑節度使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, with the acting title Minister of Rites, he went out as military commissioner of Zheng-Hua.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, with acting rank as Minister of Rites, Deyu was sent out as commissioner of Zheng-Hua.

sentences.zh: 德裕為逢吉所擯，在浙西八年。

translations.literal: Deyu had been driven out by Fengji and remained in western Zhe eight years.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu, ostracized by Fengji, stayed in western Zhe eight years.

sentences.zh: 雖遠闕庭，每上章言事。

translations.literal: Though far from the court, he often submitted memorials on affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: Though distant from court, he often memorialized on public affairs.

sentences.zh: 文宗素知忠藎，采朝論征之。

translations.literal: Wenzong had long known his loyalty and devotion and, taking court opinion, summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong had long known his loyalty and, heeding court opinion, recalled him.

sentences.zh: 到未旬時，又為宗閔所逐，中懷於悒，無以自申。

translations.literal: Within less than ten days after his arrival he was again driven out by Zongmin; bitterness filled his breast and he had no way to explain himself.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days of arrival he was again expelled by Zongmin; resentment filled him and he had no way to clear himself.

sentences.zh: 賴鄭覃侍講禁中，時稱其善；

translations.literal: Fortunately Zheng Tan lectured within the Forbidden Precinct and was then praised for his goodness;
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately Zheng Tan lectured in the inner palace and was praised for his integrity;

sentences.zh: 雖朋黨流言，帝乃心未已。

translations.literal: though factional slander spread, the emperor's heart was not yet spent.
translations.idiomatic: though factional rumor swirled, the emperor's regard for him did not die.

sentences.zh: 宗閔尋引牛僧孺同知政事，二憾相結，凡德裕之善者，皆斥之於外。

translations.literal: Zongmin soon brought in Niu Sengru as co-administrator of the government; the two grudges joined, and whatever favored Deyu was cast out abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Zongmin soon brought Niu Sengru in as fellow chancellor; the two grievances fused, and anyone who favored Deyu was pushed out of court.

sentences.zh: 四年十月，以德裕檢校兵部尚書、成都尹、劍南西川節度副大使、知節度事、管內觀察處置、西山八國雲南招撫等使。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourth year, Deyu was made acting Minister of War, Prefect of Chengdu, deputy military commissioner of Jiannan West Circuit with control of circuit affairs, intramural observation and disposition commissioner, and commissioner for pacification of the Eight Kingdoms of the Western Mountains, Yunnan, and related posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of year 4, Deyu was made acting Minister of War, Prefect of Chengdu, Jiannan West Circuit deputy commissioner with full circuit authority, observation commissioner within the circuit, and commissioner for the Western Mountain Eight Kingdoms, Yunnan pacification, and related duties.

sentences.zh: 裴度於宗閔有恩。

translations.literal: Pei Du owed Zongmin a favor.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du was in Zongmin's debt.

sentences.zh: 度征淮西時，請宗閔為彰義觀察判官，自後名位日進。

translations.literal: When Du campaigned in Huai-Xi, he had asked Zongmin to serve as Zhangyi observation judge; from then on Zongmin's name and rank rose day by day.
translations.idiomatic: During Du's Huai-Xi campaign he had appointed Zongmin Zhangyi observation judge; thereafter Zongmin's rank rose steadily.

sentences.zh: 至是恨度援德裕，罷度相位，出為興元節度使，牛、李權赫於天下。

translations.literal: By then he resented Du for backing Deyu, removed Du from the chancellorship, and sent him out as Xingyuan military commissioner; Niu and Li then towered over the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Now he resented Du for supporting Deyu, stripped Du of the chancellorship, and sent him to Xingyuan; Niu and Li then dominated the empire.

sentences.zh: 西川承蠻寇剽虜之後，郭釗撫理無術，人不聊生。

translations.literal: In western Shu, after the ravages of the Man raiders, Guo Zhao's governance had no method and the people could scarcely live.
translations.idiomatic: Western Shu, after Man raids and plunder, had been ruled without skill by Guo Zhao; the people were destitute.

sentences.zh: 德裕乃復葺關防，繕完兵守。

translations.literal: Deyu then restored the passes and defenses and repaired the troops and garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu restored frontier posts and defenses and put the army and garrisons back in order.

sentences.zh: 又遣人入南詔，求其所俘工匠，得僧道工巧四千余人，復歸成都。

translations.literal: He also sent men into Nanzhao to seek the craftsmen it had captured, obtaining more than four thousand monks, artisans, and skilled workers and bringing them back to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent envoys into Nanzhao to recover captured craftsmen, obtaining more than four thousand monks, artisans, and skilled workers and restoring them to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 五年九月，吐蕃維州守將悉怛謀請以城降。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fifth year, the Tibetan garrison commander of Weizhou, Xin Tuanmo, asked to surrender the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of year 5, the Tibetan garrison commander of Weizhou, Xin Tuanmo, offered to surrender the city.

sentences.zh: 其州南界江陽，岷山連嶺而西，不知其極；

translations.literal: South of the prefecture it bordered Jiangyang; westward the Min Mountains ran in linked ridges without end.
translations.idiomatic: South of the prefecture lay Jiangyang; westward the Min Mountains stretched in endless ridges.

sentences.zh: 北望隴山，積雪如玉；

translations.literal: Looking north one saw Long Mountains, snow piled like jade.
translations.idiomatic: To the north one saw Long Mountains, snow heaped like jade.

sentences.zh: 東望成都，若在井底。

translations.literal: Looking east one saw Chengdu as if from the bottom of a well.
translations.idiomatic: To the east one saw Chengdu as though from the bottom of a well.

sentences.zh: 一面孤峰，三面臨江，是西蜀控吐蕃之要地。

translations.literal: One face was a lone peak; three faces faced the river—it was the key ground by which western Shu controlled Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: One side was a lone peak; three sides faced the river—the choke point by which western Shu held Tibet at bay.

sentences.zh: 至德後，河、隴陷蕃，唯此州尚存。

translations.literal: After Zhide, He and Long fell to Tibet; only this prefecture remained.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhide, the He and Long regions fell to Tibet; only this prefecture remained.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃利險要，將婦人嫁於此州閽者。

translations.literal: Tibet prized its strategic strength and married women to the gatekeepers of this prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet prized its terrain and married women to the men who kept its gates.

sentences.zh: 二十年後，婦人生二子成長。

translations.literal: Twenty years later the women bore two sons who grew to manhood.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty years on, the women bore two sons who came of age.

sentences.zh: 及蕃兵攻城，二子內應，其州遂陷。

translations.literal: When Tibetan troops attacked the city, the two sons responded from within and the prefecture fell.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibetan troops besieged the city, the two sons opened from within and the prefecture was lost.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃得之，號曰「無憂城」。

translations.literal: Tibet took it and called it the "City Without Sorrow."
translations.idiomatic: Tibet took it and named it the "City Without Care."

sentences.zh: 貞元中，韋臯鎮蜀，經略西山八國，萬計取之不獲，至是悉怛謀遣人送款。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyuan era, Wei Gao governed Shu and campaigned against the Eight Kingdoms of the Western Mountains; though he mustered ten thousand stratagems he could not recover it—now Xin Tuanmo sent envoys offering submission.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhenyuan, Wei Gao held Shu and campaigned against the Western Mountain Eight Kingdoms; with ten thousand schemes he could not retake it—now Xin Tuanmo sent men to offer allegiance.

sentences.zh: 德裕疑其詐，遣人送錦袍金帶與之，托雲候取進止，悉怛謀乃盡率郡人歸成都。

translations.literal: Deyu suspected deception, sent men with a brocade robe and gold belt, feigning that he awaited orders on how to proceed; Xin Tuanmo then led all the people of the prefecture back to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu suspected a ruse and sent envoys with a brocade robe and gold belt, claiming he was waiting for instructions; Xin Tuanmo then brought the entire prefecture back to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 德裕乃發兵鎮守，因陳出攻之利害。

translations.literal: Deyu then deployed troops to garrison and defend, and submitted a memorial setting forth the advantages and disadvantages of launching an attack.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu then sent troops to secure the region and memorialized on the gains and risks of an offensive.

sentences.zh: 時牛僧孺沮議，言新與吐蕃結盟，不宜敗約，語在《僧孺傳》。

translations.literal: At the time Niu Sengru obstructed the plan, saying they had recently allied with Tibet and should not break the treaty—the account is in his biography.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Sengru blocked the proposal, arguing that Tibet had just become an ally and the pact must not be broken; the fuller account is in his biography.

sentences.zh: 乃詔德裕卻送悉怛謀一部之人還維州，贊普得之，皆加虐刑。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered Deyu to send back Xin Tuanmo's followers to Weizhou; when the btsan-po got them, he imposed cruel punishments on all.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered Deyu to return Xin Tuanmo's people to Weizhou; when the Tibetan king received them, he inflicted savage punishments on them all.

sentences.zh: 德裕六年復修邛峽關，移巂州於臺登城以扞蠻。

translations.literal: In Deyu's sixth year he again repaired Qiong Gorge Pass and moved Xi Prefecture to Taideng walled city to hold the Man at bay.
translations.idiomatic: In his sixth year in command he rebuilt Qiong Gorge Pass and moved Xi Prefecture to Taideng to block the southern tribes.

sentences.zh: 德裕所歷征鎮，以政績聞。

translations.literal: Every military commission Deyu held became known for his administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: In every post as frontier commissioner, his governance won renown.

sentences.zh: 其在蜀也，西拒吐蕃，南平蠻、蜒。

translations.literal: In Shu he held Tibet at bay in the west and pacified the Man and Yan in the south.
translations.idiomatic: In Shu he checked Tibet in the west and pacified the Man and Yan peoples in the south.

sentences.zh: 數年之內，夜犬不驚；

translations.literal: Within a few years, dogs did not bark at night.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years the nights were so quiet that dogs never barked.

sentences.zh: 瘡痏之民，粗以完復。

translations.literal: The people, wounded like running sores, were roughly restored to wholeness.
translations.idiomatic: A populace scarred by war was brought, however roughly, back to wholeness.

sentences.zh: 會監軍王踐言入朝知樞密，嘗於上前言悉怛謀縛送以快戎心，絕歸降之義，上頗尤僧孺。

translations.literal: When supervising army commissioner Wang Jianyan entered court as Privy Council director, he once told the emperor before him that binding and sending Xin Tuanmo pleased the barbarians' hearts and cut off the meaning of surrender; the emperor greatly blamed Sengru.
translations.idiomatic: When army supervisor Wang Jianyan entered court to serve on the Privy Council, he told the emperor that handing Xin Tuanmo over in bonds had gratified the Tibetans and destroyed the logic of defection; the emperor came to blame Sengru deeply.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，召德裕為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: That winter Deyu was summoned as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Deyu was recalled as Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 僧孺罷相，出為淮南節度使。

translations.literal: Sengru left the chancellorship and went out as Huainan military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Sengru was removed from the chancellorship and sent out to govern Huainan.

sentences.zh: 七年二月，德裕以本官平章事，進封贊皇伯，食邑七百戶。

translations.literal: In the second month of year 7, Deyu became chief minister in his existing post, was advanced to Baron of Zanhuang, with a fief of seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year 7 he became chief minister while keeping his existing rank, was ennobled as Baron of Zanhuang, and received a fief of seven hundred households.

sentences.zh: 六月，宗閔亦罷，德裕代為中書侍郎、集賢大學士。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Zongmin also left office; Deyu replaced him as Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Academician of the Hall for Cherishing Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Zongmin was dismissed as well; Deyu took his place as Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Academician of the Hall for Cherishing Worthies.

sentences.zh: 其年十二月，文宗暴風恙，不能言者月余。

translations.literal: That twelfth month Emperor Wenzong suddenly fell gravely ill and could not speak for more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of that year Wenzong was stricken with a sudden violent illness and remained speechless for more than a month.

sentences.zh: 八年正月十六日，始力疾御紫宸見百僚。

translations.literal: On the sixteenth day of the first month of year 8, he at last forced himself, ill, to preside in Zichen and receive the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixteenth day of the first month of year 8 he at last dragged himself, still ill, to the Zichen Hall to face the full court.

sentences.zh: 宰臣退問安否，上嘆醫無名工者久之。

translations.literal: The chief ministers withdrew and inquired after his health; the emperor sighed long that there was no famed physician of skill.
translations.idiomatic: When the chief ministers withdrew and asked after his health, the emperor sighed at length that no master physician could be found.

sentences.zh: 由是王守澄進鄭註。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wang Shoucheng presented Zheng Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Wang Shoucheng introduced Zheng Zhu.

sentences.zh: 初，註構宋申錫事，帝深惡之，欲令京兆尹杖殺之。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhu had framed the Song Shenxi affair; the emperor deeply hated him and wished to have the Jingzhao prefect beat him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhu had engineered the Song Shenxi affair; the emperor loathed him and wanted the Jingzhao prefect to beat him to death.

sentences.zh: 至是以藥稍效，始善遇之。

translations.literal: Now that the medicine was somewhat effective, he began to treat him kindly.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the medicine was beginning to work, the emperor started to treat him with favor.

sentences.zh: 守澄復進李訓，善《易》。

translations.literal: Shoucheng also presented Li Xun, skilled in the Book of Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Shoucheng also introduced Li Xun, who was adept in the Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 其年秋，上欲授訓諫官。

translations.literal: That autumn the emperor wished to appoint Xun as remonstrance official.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the emperor wished to make Xun a remonstrance official.

sentences.zh: 德裕奏曰：「李訓小人，不可在陛下左右。

translations.literal: Deyu memorialized: "Li Xun is a petty man and must not be at Your Majesty's side.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu submitted: "Li Xun is a base man and must not remain at Your Majesty's side.

sentences.zh: 頃年惡積，天下皆知；

translations.literal: His wickedness has piled up these past years and all the realm knows it;
translations.idiomatic: His misdeeds have accumulated for years and the whole empire knows them;

sentences.zh: 無故用之，必駭視聽。」

translations.literal: to employ him without cause would surely alarm eyes and ears."
translations.idiomatic: to appoint him without cause would shock every eye and ear in the realm."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「人誰無過，俟其悛改。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Who has no faults? Wait until he reforms.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Who is without fault? Let him reform first.

sentences.zh: 朕以逢吉所托，不忍負言。」

translations.literal: I, because of what Fengji entrusted, cannot bear to fail his word."
translations.idiomatic: I cannot, for Fengji's sake, break the pledge he entrusted to me."

sentences.zh: 德裕曰：「聖人有改過之義。

translations.literal: Deyu said, "The sage has the principle of reforming faults.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu said, "Even sages hold that faults may be corrected.

sentences.zh: 訓天性奸邪，無悛改之理。」

translations.literal: Xun's nature is treacherous and vile; there is no principle of reform in him."
translations.idiomatic: But Xun is treacherous by nature; there is no reform in him."

sentences.zh: 上顧王涯曰：「商量別與一官。」

translations.literal: The emperor turned to Wang Ya and said, "Discuss and give him some other office."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to Wang Ya and said, "Find him some other post."

sentences.zh: 遂授四門助教。

translations.literal: He was then appointed tutor of the Four Gates.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was then made tutor of the Four Gates.

sentences.zh: 制出，給事中鄭肅、韓佽封之不下。

translations.literal: When the appointment order issued, the supervising secretaries Zheng Su and Han Yi sealed it and would not release it.
translations.idiomatic: When the appointment edict was issued, the supervising secretaries Zheng Su and Han Yi sealed it and refused to promulgate it.

sentences.zh: 王涯召肅面喻令下。

translations.literal: Wang Ya summoned Su face to face and instructed him to release it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ya summoned Su and instructed him in person to let it through.

sentences.zh: 俄而鄭註亦自絳州至。

translations.literal: Before long Zheng Zhu also arrived from Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zheng Zhu too arrived from Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 訓、註惡德裕排己，九月十日，復召宗閔於興元，授中書侍郎、平章事，代德裕。

translations.literal: Xun and Zhu hated Deyu for blocking them; on the tenth day of the ninth month Zongmin was again summoned from Xingyuan, made Vice Director and chief minister, replacing Deyu.
translations.idiomatic: Xun and Zhu resented Deyu for shutting them out; on the tenth day of the ninth month Zongmin was recalled from Xingyuan, made Vice Director and chief minister, and replaced Deyu.

sentences.zh: 出德裕為興元節度使。

translations.literal: Deyu was sent out as Xingyuan military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu was sent out to serve as Xingyuan military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 德裕中謝日，自陳戀闕，不願出籓，追敕守兵部尚書。

translations.literal: On the day Deyu took leave in the inner court he stated his attachment to the throne and unwillingness to leave the frontier; an urgent edict followed keeping him as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: At his court leave-taking Deyu declared his longing for the capital and his unwillingness to go to the provinces; an urgent edict followed, leaving him Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 宗閔奏制命已行，不宜自便，尋改檢校尚書左僕射、潤州刺史、鎮海軍節度、蘇常杭潤觀察等使，代王璠。

translations.literal: Zongmin memorialized that the appointment edict had already been promulgated and he should not act for his own convenience; soon he was changed to acting Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, Prefect of Runzhou, Zhenhai army commissioner, Suzhou-Changzhou-Hangzhou-Runzhou observation commissioner, and related posts, replacing Wang Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Zongmin argued that the appointment had already been issued and Deyu must not bend the rules to suit himself; he was soon changed to acting Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, Prefect of Runzhou, Zhenhai military commissioner, and Suzhou-Changzhou-Hangzhou-Runzhou observation commissioner, replacing Wang Pu.

sentences.zh: 德裕至鎮，奉詔安排宮人杜仲陽於道觀，與之供給。

translations.literal: When Deyu reached his post he followed an edict to arrange Palace Woman Du Zhongyang in a Daoist abbey and provided for her.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his command Deyu carried out an edict placing palace woman Du Zhongyang in a Daoist abbey and supplying her needs.

sentences.zh: 仲陽者，漳王養母，王得罪，放仲陽於潤州故也。

translations.literal: Zhongyang was the foster mother of Prince Zhang; when the prince was punished, Zhongyang was released to Runzhou for that reason.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyang had been Prince Zhang's nurse; when the prince fell, she had been sent down to Runzhou for that reason.

sentences.zh: 九年三月，左丞王璠、戶部侍郎李漢進狀，論德裕在鎮，厚賂仲陽，結托漳王，圖為不軌。

translations.literal: In the third month of year 9, Left Assistant Wang Pu and Vice Minister of Revenue Li Han submitted a memorial accusing Deyu at his post of richly bribing Zhongyang and colluding with Prince Zhang to plot rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year 9, Left Assistant Wang Pu and Vice Minister of Revenue Li Han memorialized that at his post Deyu had lavished bribes on Zhongyang and conspired with Prince Zhang to rebel.

sentences.zh: 四月，帝於蓬萊殿召王涯、李固言、路隨、王璠、李漢、鄭註等，面證其事。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the emperor at Penglai Hall summoned Wang Ya, Li Guyan, Lu Sui, Wang Pu, Li Han, Zheng Zhu, and others to examine the matter face to face.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the emperor summoned Wang Ya, Li Guyan, Lu Sui, Wang Pu, Li Han, Zheng Zhu, and others to Penglai Hall to confront the charges.

sentences.zh: 璠、漢加誣構結，語甚切至。

translations.literal: Pu and Han piled on false accusations of collusion, their words extremely pointed.
translations.idiomatic: Pu and Han heaped on fabricated charges of conspiracy, their language fierce and exact.

sentences.zh: 路隨奏曰：「德裕實不至此。

translations.literal: Lu Sui memorialized: "Deyu truly has not come to this.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Sui submitted: "Deyu has surely not gone so far.

sentences.zh: 誠如璠、漢之言，僥臣亦合得罪。」

translations.literal: If it is as Pu and Han say, your humble servant too should be guilty."
translations.idiomatic: If what Pu and Han say is true, your unworthy servant deserves punishment as well."

sentences.zh: 群論稍息。

translations.literal: The clamor gradually subsided.
translations.idiomatic: The uproar gradually died away.

sentences.zh: 尋授德裕太子賓客，分懷東都。

translations.literal: Soon Deyu was made Crown Prince's guest and assigned to the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Deyu was made Crown Prince's guest and posted to the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 其月，又貶袁州長史。

translations.literal: That same month he was demoted to Registrar of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That same month he was demoted to registrar of Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 路隨坐證德裕，罷相，出鎮浙西。

translations.literal: Lu Sui, for testifying for Deyu, was removed from the chancellorship and sent to govern western Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Sui, for speaking up for Deyu, was stripped of the chancellorship and sent out to govern western Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 其年七月，宗閔坐救楊虞卿，貶處州。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of that year Zongmin, for saving Yang Yuqing, was demoted to Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of that year Zongmin, for intervening for Yang Yuqing, was demoted to Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 李漢坐黨宗閔，貶汾州。

translations.literal: Li Han, for partisanship with Zongmin, was demoted to Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Han, as Zongmin's partisan, was demoted to Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 十一月，王璠與李訓造亂伏誅，而文宗深悟前事，知德裕為朋黨所誣。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Wang Pu and Li Xun made rebellion and were executed; Emperor Wenzong came deeply to understand the earlier affair and knew Deyu had been slandered by faction.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Wang Pu and Li Xun rose in rebellion and were executed; Wenzong then saw the earlier case clearly and knew Deyu had been framed by faction.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，授德裕銀青光祿大夫，量移滁州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third month of the next year Deyu was given Silver and Blue Light Chamberlain and transferred in grade to Prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the following year Deyu was made Silver and Blue Light Chamberlain and transferred in grade to prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 七月，遷太子賓客。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he was moved to Crown Prince's guest.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was made Crown Prince's guest again.

sentences.zh: 十一月，檢校戶部尚書，復浙西觀察使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month acting Minister of Revenue and restored western Zhejiang observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was made acting Minister of Revenue and restored as western Zhejiang observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 德裕凡三鎮浙西，前後十余年。

translations.literal: Deyu in all thrice governed western Zhejiang, more than ten years in total.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu governed western Zhejiang three times in all, for more than ten years altogether.

sentences.zh: 開成二年五月，授揚州大都督府長史、淮南節度副大使、知節度使事，代牛僧孺。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of Kai Cheng year 2, he was made Yangzhou metropolitan-area chief administrator, Huainan deputy military commissioner with control of circuit affairs, replacing Niu Sengru.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Kai Cheng year 2 he was made chief administrator of the Yangzhou metropolitan prefecture, Huainan deputy commissioner with full circuit authority, replacing Niu Sengru.

sentences.zh: 初，僧孺聞德裕代己，乃以軍府事交付副使張鷺，即時入朝。

translations.literal: Initially when Sengru heard Deyu would replace him, he handed military headquarters affairs to deputy commissioner Zhang Lu and immediately entered court.
translations.idiomatic: When Sengru first learned Deyu would replace him, he handed headquarters affairs to deputy commissioner Zhang Lu and hurried to court.

sentences.zh: 時揚州府藏錢帛八十萬貫匹，及德裕至鎮，奏領得止四十萬，半為張鷺支用訖。

translations.literal: At the time Yangzhou treasury held eight hundred thousand strings and bolts of cash and silk; when Deyu reached his post he memorialized receiving only four hundred thousand—half had been spent by Zhang Lu.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangzhou treasury then held eight hundred thousand strings and pieces of cash and silk; when Deyu took command he reported receiving only four hundred thousand—half had already been spent by Zhang Lu.

sentences.zh: 僧孺上章訟其事，詔德裕重檢括，果如僧孺之數。

translations.literal: Sengru submitted a memorial disputing the matter; an edict ordered Deyu to re-audit; it matched Sengru's figures.
translations.idiomatic: Sengru memorialized to dispute the account; the court ordered Deyu to audit again, and the total matched Sengru's.

sentences.zh: 德裕稱初到鎮疾病，為吏隱欺，請罰。

translations.literal: Deyu said on first reaching his post he was ill and his clerks concealed and deceived him; he asked punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu said that when he first arrived he had been ill and his clerks had concealed the truth; he asked to be punished.

sentences.zh: 詔釋之。

translations.literal: An edict pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict excused him.

sentences.zh: 補闕王績、魏謨，崔黨韋有翼、拾遺令狐綯書左僕射。

translations.literal: The remonstrance officials Wang Ji and Wei Mo, the Cui partisan Wei Youyi, and the remonstrance official Linghu Tao submitted memorials to the Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The remonstrance officials Wang Ji and Wei Mo, the Cui partisan Wei Youyi, and the remonstrance official Linghu Tao all memorialized the Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，武宗即位。

translations.literal: In the first month of year 5, Wuzong ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 5 Wuzong ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 七月，召德裕於淮南。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Deyu was summoned from Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Deyu was recalled from Huainan.

sentences.zh: 九月，授門下侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was made Vice Director of the Chancellery and Fellow Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was made Vice Director of the Chancellery and fellow chief minister.

sentences.zh: 初，德裕父吉甫，年五十一出鎮淮南，五十四自淮南復相。

translations.literal: Earlier Deyu's father Jifu at age fifty-one went out to govern Huainan; at fifty-four he returned from Huainan to the chancellorship again.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Deyu's father Jifu had gone out to govern Huainan at fifty-one and returned from Huainan to the chancellorship at fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 今德裕鎮淮南，復入相，一如父之年，亦為異事。

translations.literal: Now Deyu governed Huainan and re-entered the chancellorship at the same ages as his father—a singular thing.
translations.idiomatic: Now Deyu governed Huainan and re-entered the chancellorship at the same ages—a remarkable echo of his father.

sentences.zh: 會昌元年，兼左僕射。

translations.literal: In Huichang year 1 he concurrently held Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In Huichang year 1 he also served as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 開成末，回紇為黠戛斯所攻。

translations.literal: At the end of Kai Cheng, the Uyghurs were attacked by the Kirghiz.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Kai Cheng era the Uyghurs were attacked by the Kirghiz.

sentences.zh: 戰敗，部族離散。

translations.literal: Defeated in battle, their tribes scattered.
translations.idiomatic: They were defeated in battle and their tribes scattered.

sentences.zh: 烏介可汗奉太和公主南來。

translations.literal: Khan Wujie led Princess Taihe south.
translations.idiomatic: Khan Wujie escorted Princess Taihe south.

sentences.zh: 會昌二年二月，牙於塞上，遣使求助兵糧，收復本國，權借天德軍以安公主。

translations.literal: In February of Huichang year 2, encamped on the frontier, he sent envoys requesting troops and grain to recover his state, and asked to borrow the Tiande Army temporarily to secure the princess.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Huichang year 2, encamped on the frontier, he sent envoys to beg troops and grain to recover his realm and asked to borrow the Tiande Army temporarily to protect the princess.

sentences.zh: 時天德軍使田牟，請以沙陁、退渾諸部落兵擊之。

translations.literal: The Tiande commissioner Tian Mou asked to strike with Shatuo and Tuyuhun tribal forces.
translations.idiomatic: The Tiande commissioner Tian Mou asked to attack with Shatuo and Tuyuhun tribal troops.

sentences.zh: 上意未決，下百僚商議，議者多雲如牟之奏。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was undecided; he sent it down for the hundred officials to discuss; most said to follow Mou's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had not decided; he referred the matter to the hundred officials, and most favored Mou's proposal.

sentences.zh: 德裕曰：「頃者國家艱難之際，回紇繼立大功。

translations.literal: Deyu said: "Not long ago in the state's time of hardship the Uyghurs stood great merit.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu said: "In the empire's recent straits the Uyghurs rendered great service.

sentences.zh: 今國破家亡，竄投無所，自居塞上，未至侵淫。

translations.literal: Now state destroyed and house lost, they flee with nowhere to go, camped on the frontier themselves—not yet reaching violation and encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: Now their state is broken and their house ruined; they wander with nowhere to turn, encamped on the frontier themselves—they have not yet crossed into outright aggression.

sentences.zh: 以窮來歸，遽行殺伐，非漢宣待呼韓邪之道也。

translations.literal: To kill and strike when they come in desperation is not the Way of Han Xuandi treating Hu Hanxie.
translations.idiomatic: To slaughter them the moment they come in desperation is not the way Emperor Xuan of Han treated Hu Hanxie.

sentences.zh: 不如聊濟資糧，徐觀其變。」

translations.literal: Better briefly to supply provisions and grain and watch their changes slowly."
translations.idiomatic: Better to supply them with provisions for the moment and watch how matters develop."

sentences.zh: 宰相陳夷行曰：「此借寇兵而資盜糧，非計也，不如擊之便。」

translations.literal: Chief Minister Chen Yixing said, "This is to lend the enemy troops and feed bandit grain—not a plan; better to strike at once."
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Chen Yixing said, "That is to arm the foe and feed the robber—no strategy at all. Strike them at once."

sentences.zh: 德裕曰：「田牟、韋仲平言沙陀、退渾並願擊賊，此緩急不可恃也。

translations.literal: Deyu said, "Tian Mou and Wei Zhongping say Shatuo and Tuyuhun all wish to strike the rebels—this is not to be relied on in urgency or slackness.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu said, "Tian Mou and Wei Zhongping claim the Shatuo and Tuyuhun are eager to attack the enemy, but that cannot be trusted in a crisis.

sentences.zh: 夫見利則進，遇敵則散，是雜虜之常態，必不肯為國家扞禦邊境。

translations.literal: When they see profit they advance; when they meet the enemy they scatter—this is the constant manner of mixed barbarians; they surely will not willing defend the border for the state.
translations.idiomatic: They advance when they see gain and scatter when they meet the foe—that is the usual way of mixed tribes; they will never truly hold the frontier for the state.

sentences.zh: 天德一城，戍兵寡弱，而欲與勁虜結讎，陷之必矣。

translations.literal: Tiande is one city, garrison troops few and weak, yet you wish to make an enemy of a fierce barbarian—certainly it will be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Tiande is a single weakly garrisoned city, yet you would make an enemy of a fierce foe—it will surely be lost.

sentences.zh: 不如以理恤之，俟其越軼，用兵為便。」

translations.literal: Better to comfort them with reason; wait until they overstep bounds, then use troops is convenient."
translations.idiomatic: Better to treat them fairly for now; when they overstep their bounds, then military action will be the better course."

sentences.zh: 帝以為然，許借米三萬石。

translations.literal: The emperor thought it right and permitted lending thirty thousand shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and authorized lending thirty thousand shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 俄而回紇宰相霡沒斯殺赤心宰相，以其眾來降。

translations.literal: Soon Uyghur chancellor Meilis killed the Chixin chancellor and brought his hosts to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Uyghur chancellor Meilis killed the Chixin chancellor and came over with his followers.

sentences.zh: 赤心部族又投幽州。

translations.literal: The Chixin tribes again fled to Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Chixin tribes in turn fled to Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 烏介勢孤，而不與之米，其眾饑乏，漸近振武保大柵、杷頭峰，突入朔州州界。

translations.literal: Wujie was isolated; without grain given his hosts were hungry and depleted, gradually approaching Zhenwu's Baoda strongpoint and Batou Peak, bursting into Shuozhou's border.
translations.idiomatic: Wujie stood alone; denied grain, his men grew hungry and weak, drifted toward Zhenwu's Baoda stockade and Batou Peak, and broke into Shuozhou's territory.

sentences.zh: 沙陁、退渾皆以其家保山險；

translations.literal: Shatuo and Tuyuhun all sheltered their families in mountain fastnesses;
translations.idiomatic: The Shatuo and Tuyuhun all hid their families in mountain strongholds;

sentences.zh: 雲州張獻節嬰城自固。

translations.literal: Yunzhou's Zhang Xianjie held his walled city and defended himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xianjie at Yunzhou shut his walls and held out.

sentences.zh: 虜大縱掠，卒無拒者。

translations.literal: The barbarians plundered widely; in the end none resisted.
translations.idiomatic: The invaders looted at will; in the end no one stood against them.

sentences.zh: 上憂之，與宰臣計事。

translations.literal: The emperor was worried and discussed affairs with chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was alarmed and took counsel with his chancellors.

sentences.zh: 德裕曰：「杷頭峰北，便是沙磧，彼中野戰，須用騎兵。

translations.literal: Deyu said: "North of Batou Peak lies sandy desert; for field battle there one needs cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu said: "North of Batou Peak is open desert; fighting there requires cavalry.

sentences.zh: 若以步卒敵之，理難必勝。

translations.literal: If infantry opposes them, reason makes victory hard.
translations.idiomatic: Pitting foot soldiers against them, victory is hard to secure by any logic.

sentences.zh: 今烏介所恃者公主，如令勇將出奇奪得公主，虜自敗矣。」

translations.literal: Now what Wujie relies on is the princess; if brave generals take her by surprise, the barbarians will defeat themselves."
