translations.idiomatic: Wujie's strength is the princess; send bold commanders to seize her by surprise and the enemy will collapse of itself."

sentences.zh: 上然之，即令德裕草制處分代北諸軍，固關防，以出奇形勢授劉沔。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed and at once ordered Deyu to draft an edict disposing the northern armies, securing passes, giving Liu Mian authority for surprise operations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented and at once ordered Deyu to draft an edict directing the northern armies, tightening the passes, and entrusting Liu Mian with a surprise strategy.

sentences.zh: 沔令大將石雄急擊可汗於殺胡山；

translations.literal: Mian ordered great general Shi Xiong to strike the khan urgently at Kill-the-Hun Mountain;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian ordered his great general Shi Xiong to strike the khan swiftly at Kill-the-Hun Mountain;

sentences.zh: 敗之，迎公主還宮，語在《石雄傳》。

translations.literal: defeated him and welcomed the princess back to the palace—the account is in Shi's biography.
translations.idiomatic: defeated him and escorted the princess back to the palace—the fuller account is in Shi's biography.

sentences.zh: 尋進位司空。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，趙蕃奏黠戛斯攻安西、北庭都護府，宜出師應援。

translations.literal: In the second month of year 3, Zhao Fan memorialized that the Kirghiz attacked the Anxi and Beiting protectorates and troops should be sent in support.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year 3 Zhao Fan memorialized that the Kirghiz were attacking the Anxi and Beiting protectorates and that an army should be sent to their aid.

sentences.zh: 德裕奏曰：

translations.literal: Deyu memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Deyu submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 帝意傷之，尋賜贈官。

translations.literal: The emperor's heart was moved with grief, and soon he granted posthumous honors.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply grieved and soon bestowed posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 其年，德裕兼守司徒。

translations.literal: That year Deyu also served concurrently as Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: That year Deyu was additionally appointed acting Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 四月，澤潞節度使劉從諫卒，軍人以其侄稹擅總留後，三軍請降旄鉞。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the Zelu military governor Liu Congjian died; the troops, with his nephew Zhen seizing control of the acting governorship on his own authority, asked that the imperial banner and axe be lowered to them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Liu Congjian, military governor of Zelu, died. The army had his nephew Liu Zhen take charge of the post on his own, and the three armies petitioned for the commission of command.

sentences.zh: 帝與宰臣議可否，德裕曰：「澤潞國家內地，不同河朔。

translations.literal: The emperor discussed with chief ministers whether to approve it; Deyu said: "Zelu is inner territory of the state, not like Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took counsel with his chancellors on whether to grant the request. Deyu said: "Zelu lies within the empire's heartland, unlike the Hebei circuits.

sentences.zh: 前後命帥，皆用儒臣。

translations.literal: Successive appointments as commander all used Confucian officials.
translations.idiomatic: Every prior appointment to command had gone to scholar-officials.

sentences.zh: 頃者李抱真成立此軍，身歿之後，德宗尚不許繼襲，令李緘護喪歸洛。

translations.literal: Not long ago Li Baozhen founded this army; after his death Dezong still would not allow succession and ordered Li Jian to escort the coffin back to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Baozhen first raised this army, Dezong after his death still refused hereditary succession and sent Li Jian to escort the funeral train to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 洎劉悟作鎮，長慶中頗亦自專。

translations.literal: When Liu Wu became governor, in the Changqing era he too was rather self-willed.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Liu Wu held the post, in the Changqing years he had grown quite autonomous.

sentences.zh: 屬敬宗因循，遂許從諫繼襲。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Jingzong's indulgence, Congjian's succession was eventually allowed.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong's lax rule allowed Congjian to inherit in the end.

sentences.zh: 開成初，於長子屯軍，欲興晉陽之甲，以除君側；

translations.literal: At the start of Kai Cheng he stationed troops at his eldest son's command, intending to raise the armies of Jinyang to purge the emperor's flank;
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kai Cheng he massed troops at his eldest son's base, planning to raise Jinyang's armies to cleanse the court;

sentences.zh: 與鄭註、李訓交結至深，外托效忠，實懷窺伺。

translations.literal: he was deeply tied with Zheng Zhu and Li Xun, outwardly professing loyalty while inwardly harboring designs of watching for opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: he was intimate with Zheng Zhu and Li Xun, pledging loyalty in public while secretly watching for his chance.

sentences.zh: 自疾病之初，便令劉稹管兵馬。

translations.literal: From the first of his illness he had Liu Zhen manage troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as illness took him he put Liu Zhen in charge of the army.

sentences.zh: 若不加討伐，何以號令四方？

translations.literal: If we do not punish him, how may we command the four quarters?
translations.idiomatic: If we do not strike, how can we command the realm?

sentences.zh: 若因循授之，則籓鎮相效，自茲威令去矣！」

translations.literal: If we indulge and grant it, the frontier commands will copy one another, and from this moment imperial authority will be gone!"
translations.idiomatic: If we indulge them and confirm the succession, every garrison will follow suit—and imperial authority will slip away forever."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿算用兵必克否？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Do you calculate that using troops will surely conquer?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked: "Do you reckon the campaign is sure to win?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「劉稹所恃者，河朔三鎮耳。

translations.literal: He replied: "What Liu Zhen relies on is only the three Hebei circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Liu Zhen's strength is nothing but the three Hebei circuits.

sentences.zh: 但得魏鎮不與稹同，破之必矣。

translations.literal: If only Weibo does not side with Zhen, breaking him is certain.
translations.idiomatic: If Weibo stays out of his camp, he can be broken for certain.

sentences.zh: 請遣重臣一人，傳達聖旨，言澤潞命帥，不同三鎮。

translations.literal: I ask that one senior minister be sent to convey the sacred intent, saying that appointments in Zelu differ from the three circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Send a senior minister to proclaim the throne's will: Zelu will receive its governor on terms unlike the three circuits.

sentences.zh: 自艱難已來，列聖皆許三鎮嗣襲，已成故事。

translations.literal: Since hardship began, successive sage emperors have all allowed the three circuits hereditary succession—it has become precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Since the troubles began, every sage emperor has allowed the three circuits to pass command from father to son—it is settled custom.

sentences.zh: 今國家欲加兵誅稹，禁軍不欲出山東。

translations.literal: Now the state wishes to send troops to execute Zhen; the imperial army does not wish to march east of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Now the court means to march against Zhen, but the central armies are reluctant to leave the capital region for the east.

sentences.zh: 其山東三州，委鎮魏出兵攻取。」

translations.literal: The three eastern prefectures should be entrusted to Weibo to raise troops and seize them."
translations.idiomatic: Let Weibo take the three eastern prefectures with its own forces."

sentences.zh: 上然之，乃令御史中丞李回使三鎮諭旨，賜魏鎮詔書云：「卿勿為子孫之謀，欲存輔車之勢。」

translations.literal: The emperor approved and ordered Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Hui to announce the intent to the three circuits; the edict to Weibo read: "Do not scheme for your descendants' sake and wish to preserve the strength of interlocking wheels."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and sent Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Hui to announce the policy to the three circuits. The edict to Weibo read: "Do not plot for your heirs and cling to the mutual grip of wagon and linchpin."

sentences.zh: 何弘敬、王元逵承詔，聳然從命。

translations.literal: He Hongjing and Wang Yuankui received the edict and straightway obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: He Hongjing and Wang Yuankui took the edict and submitted at once.

sentences.zh: 初議出兵，朝官上疏相繼，請依從諫例，許之繼襲，而宰臣四人，亦有以出師非便者。

translations.literal: When troops were first debated, court officials memorialized in succession asking that, following Congjian's precedent, succession be allowed; among the four chief ministers some also held that sending an army was inexpedient.
translations.idiomatic: At first debate court officials flooded in with memorials urging Congjian's precedent and a peaceful succession; even among the four chancellors some argued that war was unwise.

sentences.zh: 德裕奏曰：「如師出無功，臣請自當罪戾，請不累李紳、讓夷等。

translations.literal: Deyu memorialized: "If the army goes forth without success, I ask to bear the guilt myself and not involve Li Shen, Rangyi, and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu wrote: "If the campaign fails, let the blame fall on me alone—not on Li Shen, Chen Yixing, or the others.

sentences.zh: 及弘敬、元逵出兵，德裕又奏曰：「貞元、太和之間，朝廷伐叛，詔諸道會兵，才出界便費度支供餉，遲留逗撓，以困國力。

translations.literal: When Hongjing and Yuankui marched out, Deyu again memorialized: "Between Zhenyuan and Taihe, when the court campaigned against rebels, edicts summoned troops from all circuits; as soon as they crossed borders the Revenue Bureau supplied them, yet they lingered and stalled, exhausting state strength.
translations.idiomatic: " Once Hongjing and Yuankui took the field, Deyu memorialized again: "From Zhenyuan through Taihe, whenever the court suppressed rebellion it summoned allies from every circuit. The moment they crossed a border the treasury fed them—yet they dawdled and stalled until the state was drained.

sentences.zh: 或密與賊商量，取一縣一柵以為勝捷，所以師出無功。

translations.literal: Some secretly bargained with the enemy, taking one county or one stockade as victory—hence armies went forth without success.
translations.idiomatic: Some secretly dealt with the enemy, seizing a single county or stockade and calling it victory—that is why campaigns failed.

sentences.zh: 今請處分元逵、弘敬，只令收州，勿攻縣邑。」

translations.literal: Now I ask to dispose Yuankui and Hongjing: only order them to take prefectures, not attack counties and towns."
translations.idiomatic: Now restrain Yuankui and Hongjing: let them recover prefectural seats only, not ravage counties and towns."

sentences.zh: 帝然之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 及王宰、石雄進討，經年未拔澤潞。

translations.literal: When Wang Zai and Shi Xiong advanced to attack, a full year passed without taking Zelu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zai and Shi Xiong pressed the attack for a year without reducing Zelu.

sentences.zh: 及弘敬、元逵收邢、洺、磁三州，稹黨遂離，以至平殄，皆如其算。

translations.literal: When Hongjing and Yuankui recovered the three prefectures Xing, Ming, and Ci, Zhen's faction then split, until final extermination—all as he had calculated.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongjing and Yuankui recovered Xing, Ming, and Ci, Zhen's party broke apart and the rebellion was crushed—exactly as Deyu had foreseen.

sentences.zh: 時王師方討澤潞。

translations.literal: At the time the imperial army was still campaigning against Zelu.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial campaign against Zelu was still under way.

sentences.zh: 三年十二月，太原橫水戍兵因移戍榆社。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of year 3 the Hengshui garrison at Taiyuan, because of transfer to garrison Yushe,
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of year 3 the Hengshui garrison at Taiyuan, ordered to transfer to Yüshe,

sentences.zh: 乃倒戈入太原城，逐節度使李石，推其都將楊弁為留後。

translations.literal: then turned their blades, entered Taiyuan city, drove out Military Governor Li Shi, and pushed their commandant Yang Bian as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: mutinied, marched into Taiyuan, expelled Military Governor Li Shi, and made their commandant Yang Bian acting governor.

sentences.zh: 武宗以賊稹未殄，又起太原之亂，心頗憂之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong, with the rebel Zhen not yet destroyed and Taiyuan rising in turmoil, was rather worried.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong, with Liu Zhen still unbeaten and Taiyuan in revolt, grew deeply uneasy.

sentences.zh: 遣中使馬元貫往太原宣諭，覘其所為。

translations.literal: He sent Palace Envoy Ma Yuanguan to Taiyuan to proclaim and instruct and observe their conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched the palace envoy Ma Yuanguan to Taiyuan to announce the court's will and spy out the situation.

sentences.zh: 元貫受楊弁賂，欲保祐之。

translations.literal: Yuanguan accepted bribes from Yang Bian and wished to protect him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanguan took Yang Bian's bribes and meant to shield him.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，使還，奏曰：「楊弁兵馬極多，自牙門列隊至柳子，十五余裏，明光甲曳地。」

translations.literal: In the first month of year 4 the envoy returned and memorialized: "Yang Bian's troops and horses are extremely numerous; from the headquarters gate, ranks lined up to Liuzi, more than fifteen li, bright armor dragging on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: " In the first month of year 4 he returned and reported: "Yang Bian's host is immense—from the headquarters gate to Liuzi the ranks stretch more than fifteen li, bright armor sweeping the ground."

sentences.zh: 德裕奏曰：「李石比以城內無兵，抽橫水兵一千五百人赴榆社，安能朝夕間便致十五里兵甲耶？」

translations.literal: Deyu memorialized: "Li Shi lately, because the city had no troops, drew fifteen hundred Hengshui men to Yüshe—how could he in a day and night produce fifteen li of armor?"
translations.idiomatic: Deyu replied: "Li Shi, finding the city bare, had only drawn fifteen hundred Hengshui men to Yüshe—how could he overnight muster fifteen li of steel?"

sentences.zh: 元貫曰：「晉人驍敢，盡可為兵，重賞招致耳。」

translations.literal: Yuanguan said: "Jin men are fierce and bold; all can be soldiers—heavy rewards will gather them."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanguan said: "The men of Jin are fierce; any of them can fight—pay enough and they will come."

sentences.zh: 德裕曰：「招召須財，昨橫水兵亂，止為欠絹一匹。

translations.literal: Deyu said: "Recruitment requires wealth; yesterday's Hengshui mutiny was only for lack of one bolt of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu said: "Recruits cost money. Yesterday's mutiny began over a single bolt of silk owed.

sentences.zh: 李石無處得，楊弁從何致耶？

translations.literal: Li Shi had nowhere to get it—whence could Yang Bian obtain it?
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi could not pay it—where would Yang Bian find the gold?

sentences.zh: 又太原有一聯甲，並在行營，安致十五里明光耶？」

translations.literal: Moreover Taiyuan has one suit of linked armor, all with the field army—how produce fifteen li of bright armor?"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Taiyuan owns one suit of mail for the campaign army—how could fifteen li of gleaming plate appear?"

sentences.zh: 元貫詞屈。

translations.literal: Yuanguan's words were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanguan had no answer.

sentences.zh: 德裕奏曰：「楊弁微賊，決不可恕！

translations.literal: Deyu memorialized: "Yang Bian is a petty rebel and absolutely cannot be forgiven!
translations.idiomatic: " Deyu insisted: "Yang Bian is a trifling bandit and must not be spared!

sentences.zh: 如國力不及，寧舍劉稹。」

translations.literal: If state strength cannot reach so far, better abandon Liu Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: If our strength will not stretch, let Liu Zhen go—but not this man.

sentences.zh: 即時請降詔，令王逢起榆社軍，又令王元逵兵自土門入，會於太原。

translations.literal: At once he asked that an edict be issued ordering Wang Feng to raise the Yüshe army and Wang Yuankui to enter by Tumen, meeting at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately asked for edicts: Wang Feng was to rally the Yüshe troops; Wang Yuankui was to enter by Tumen and join forces at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 河東監軍呂義忠聞之，即日召榆社本道兵，誅楊弁以聞。

translations.literal: Hedong supervisory commissioner Lü Yizhong heard of it and the same day summoned the home troops of Yüshe and executed Yang Bian, reporting the fact.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong's supervisory commissioner Lü Yizhong heard and the same day called up Yüshe's native troops, killed Yang Bian, and reported success.

sentences.zh: 自開成五年冬回紇至天德，至會昌四年八月平澤潞，首尾五年，其籌度機宜，選用將帥，軍中書詔，奏請雲合，起草指蹤，皆獨決於德裕，諸相無預焉。

translations.literal: From the winter of Kai Cheng 5 when the Uyghurs reached Tiantede until the eighth month of Huichang 4 when Zelu was pacified—five years from first to last—in planning opportune moments, choosing and employing generals, military edicts and memorials clouding in, drafting orders and directing movements, all were decided solely by Deyu; the other chief ministers had no part.
translations.idiomatic: From winter of Kai Cheng 5, when the Uyghurs reached Tiantede, to the eighth month of Huichang 4, when Zelu fell—five years in all—strategy, the choice of commanders, army edicts, and the flood of memorials: every dispatch and every order was Deyu's alone. The other chancellors had no share.

sentences.zh: 以功兼守太尉，進封衛國公，三千戶。

translations.literal: For merit he also served as Grand Preceptor, was advanced to Duke of Weiguo, with three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made acting Grand Preceptor, enfeoffed as Duke of Weiguo with three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 五年，武宗上徽號後，累表乞骸，不許。

translations.literal: In year 5, after Wuzong received his honorific title, he repeatedly memorialized begging to retire; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5, after Wuzong took his honorific epithet, Deyu repeatedly asked to retire; the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 德裕病月余，堅請解機務，乃以本官平章事兼江陵尹、荊南節度使。

translations.literal: Deyu was ill more than a month and firmly asked to be relieved of state affairs; he was then made chief minister in his original rank concurrently Jingling prefect and Jingnan military governor.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month of illness he pressed to leave the Secretariat and was sent out as chief minister by title, concurrently prefect of Jiangling and military governor of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 數月追還，復知政事。

translations.literal: Several months later he was recalled and again directed state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Within months he was recalled to govern again.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，罷相，出為東都留守、東畿汝都防禦使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong ascended, he was removed from the chancellorship and sent out as Eastern Capital intendant and Eastern Metropolitan Runan defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong took the throne, Deyu was dismissed from the chancellorship and made Eastern Capital intendant and commissioner for the eastern metropolitan Runan defense.

sentences.zh: 德裕特承武宗恩顧，委以樞衡。

translations.literal: Deyu had especially received Wuzong's gracious favor and was entrusted with the pivot of power.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu had stood in Wuzong's special trust, holding the levers of power.

sentences.zh: 決策論兵，舉無遺悔，以身扞難，功流社稷。

translations.literal: In deciding policy and debating war he left nothing to regret; he bore hardship in person, and his merit flowed to the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: In counsel and in war he scarcely misstepped; he took hardship on himself, and his achievements fed the realm.

sentences.zh: 及昭肅棄天下，不逞之伍，鹹害其功。

translations.literal: When Zhaosu abandoned the world, the unruly sort all together harmed his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong died, men of malice set themselves to tear down what he had built.

sentences.zh: 白敏中、令狐綯，在會昌中德裕不以朋黨疑之，置之臺閣，顧待甚優。

translations.literal: Bai Minzhong and Linghu Tao—in Huichang Deyu had not suspected them as faction-mates and placed them in the Secretariat, treating them very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Minzhong and Linghu Tao: in Huichang Deyu had not treated them as factional foes but seated them in the Secretariat and favored them generously.

sentences.zh: 及德裕失勢，抵掌戟手，同謀斥逐，而崔鉉亦以會昌末罷相怨德裕。

translations.literal: When Deyu lost power they clapped hands and crossed spears in common plot to drive him out; Cui Xuan also, because he was dismissed from the chancellorship at the end of Huichang, resented Deyu.
translations.idiomatic: When Deyu fell they rubbed their hands and joined blades to expel him; Cui Xuan too, removed from office late in Huichang, nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 大中初，敏中復薦鉉在中書，乃相與掎摭構致，令其黨人李鹹者，訟德裕輔政時陰事。

translations.literal: At the start of Dazhong, Minzhong again recommended Xuan to the Secretariat; they then seized and fabricated charges together, setting their partisan Li Xian to sue Deyu for secret matters during his governance.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dazhong, Minzhong restored Xuan to the Secretariat; together they manufactured charges and set their man Li Xian to accuse Deyu of hidden crimes from his years in power.

sentences.zh: 乃罷德裕留守，以太子少保分司東都，時大中元年秋。

translations.literal: Deyu was then removed as intendant and made Crown Prince Junior Tutor with duty at the Eastern Capital—autumn of Dazhong year 1.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu was stripped of the intendant post and made Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince, serving at Luoyang—in the autumn of Dazhong 1.

sentences.zh: 尋再貶潮州司馬。

translations.literal: Soon he was demoted again to Chaozhou vice-prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was demoted again, to vice-prefect of Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 敏中等又令前永寧縣尉吳汝納進狀，訟李紳鎮揚州時謬斷刑獄。

translations.literal: Minzhong and the rest also had the former Yongning county lieutenant Wu Runa submit a petition suing Li Shen for wrongful judgments in criminal cases when he governed Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Minzhong's circle also had Wu Runa, former lieutenant of Yongning county, petition that Li Shen had misjudged capital cases while governing Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，又貶潮州司戶。

translations.literal: The next winter he was demoted again to Chaozhou registrar.
translations.idiomatic: The following winter he was demoted once more, to registrar of Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 德裕既貶，大中二年，自洛陽水路經江、淮赴潮州。

translations.literal: After Deyu was demoted, in Dazhong year 2 he went from Luoyang by water through the Yangtze and Huai toward Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Demoted, in Dazhong 2 he traveled from Luoyang by river through the Jiang and Huai toward Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，至潮陽，又貶崖州司戶。

translations.literal: That winter he reached Chaoyang and was demoted again to Yazhou registrar.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he reached Chaoyang and was banished farther, to registrar of Yazhou.

sentences.zh: 至三年正月，方達珠崖郡。

translations.literal: In the first month of year 3 he finally reached Zhuya commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the first month of year 3 did he reach Zhuya commandery.

sentences.zh: 十二月卒，時年六十三。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he died, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth month, at sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 德裕以器業自負，特達不群。

translations.literal: Deyu was proud of his talent and achievement, outstanding and alone in his age.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu trusted his talent and stood apart from his peers.

sentences.zh: 好著書為文，獎善嫉惡，雖位極臺輔，而讀書不輟。

translations.literal: He loved composing books and writing, rewarded good and hated evil; though he reached the summit of the Secretariat, he never ceased reading.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books and essays, honored the worthy and despised the wicked; even at the pinnacle of office he never stopped reading.

sentences.zh: 有劉三復者，長於章奏，尤奇待之。

translations.literal: There was one Liu Sanfu, skilled at memorial drafts, whom he especially favored.
translations.idiomatic: One Liu Sanfu excelled at memorial drafts and won his special regard.

sentences.zh: 自德裕始鎮浙西，迄於淮甸，皆參佐賓筵。

translations.literal: From when Deyu first governed Zhexi until the Huai region, he always joined his staff at banquets.
translations.idiomatic: From his first posting in Zhexi through the Huai campaigns, Sanfu sat at his council table.

sentences.zh: 軍政之余，與之吟詠終日。

translations.literal: Apart from military and civil affairs, he spent whole days chanting poetry with him.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond military duty they spent whole days in verse together.

sentences.zh: 在長安私第，別構起草院。

translations.literal: At his private residence in Chang'an he built a separate drafting courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: In his Chang'an mansion he built a separate drafting court.

sentences.zh: 院有精思亭；

translations.literal: In the courtyard was the Pavilion of Concentrated Thought;
translations.idiomatic: Within it stood the Pavilion of Concentrated Thought;

sentences.zh: 每朝廷用兵，詔令制置，而獨處亭中，凝然握管，左右侍者無能預焉。

translations.literal: whenever the court used troops and edicts arranged dispositions, he sat alone in the pavilion, gripping the brush in stillness, and attendants at his side could not take part.
translations.idiomatic: whenever the throne went to war and edicts had to be shaped, he sat alone in that pavilion, brush in hand, attendants barred from the work.

sentences.zh: 東都於伊闕南置平泉別墅，清流翠，樹石幽奇。

translations.literal: East of the capital, south of Yique, he set up the Pingquan villa—clear streams, green bamboo, trees and stone wondrous and secluded.
translations.idiomatic: South of Yique, east of Luoyang, he laid out the Pingquan villa: clear water, green bamboo, stone and timber strange and still.

sentences.zh: 初未仕時，講學其中。

translations.literal: Before he had entered office he lectured there.
translations.idiomatic: Before he took office he had studied there.

sentences.zh: 及從官籓服，出將入相，三十年不復重遊，而題寄歌詩，皆銘之於石。

translations.literal: After he followed office to the frontier commands, went out as general and in as minister—for thirty years he did not revisit, yet the songs and poems he sent and inscribed were all carved in stone.
translations.idiomatic: Once he marched to the provinces and returned to the council he did not walk those paths again for thirty years, yet every poem he sent back was cut into stone.

sentences.zh: 今有《花木記》、《歌詩篇錄》二石存焉。

translations.literal: Today two stones survive: the Record of Flowers and Trees and the Register of Songs and Poems.
translations.idiomatic: Two inscribed stones remain: the Record of Flowers and Trees and the Register of Songs and Poems.

sentences.zh: 有文集二十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings ran to twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 記述舊事，則有《次柳氏舊書》、《御臣要略》、《代叛志》、《獻替錄》行於世。

translations.literal: In recording old affairs there were the Sequel to the Old Writings of the Liu, Essentials for Serving Ministers, Record of Supplanting Rebellion, and Record of Offerings and Replacements circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: For history he left the Sequel to the Liu Family's Old Book, Essentials for Serving Ministers, Record of Supplanting Rebellion, and Record of Offerings and Replacements in circulation.

sentences.zh: 初貶潮州，雖蒼黃顛沛之中，猶留心著述，雜序數十篇，號曰《窮愁志》。

translations.literal: When first demoted to Chaozhou, even amid panic and ruin he still minded composition; miscellaneous prefaces numbering several tens, titled Records of Utter Want.
translations.idiomatic: Even in the first rush of exile to Chaozhou he kept writing; several dozen miscellaneous prefaces, gathered as Records of Utter Want.

sentences.zh: 其《論冥數》曰：

translations.literal: His "On Fate in the Netherworld" reads:
translations.idiomatic: His essay "On Fate in the Netherworld" begins:

sentences.zh: 其自序如此。

translations.literal: His own preface is thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his own preface.

sentences.zh: 斯論可以警夫躁競者，故書於事末。

translations.literal: This discourse may warn the rash and striving; therefore it is written at the end of the account.
translations.idiomatic: The piece is meant to warn the reckless and ambitious, and so it is set down at the close of his story.

sentences.zh: 德裕三子。

translations.literal: Deyu had three sons.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu had three sons.

sentences.zh: 燁，檢校祠部員外郎、汴宋亳觀察判官。

translations.literal: Ye, acting Vice Director of the Sacrificial Affairs Bureau and Bian-Song-Bo observation commissioner's aide.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest, Ye, served as acting Vice Director in the Sacrificial Affairs Bureau and as aide to the Bian-Song-Bo observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 大中二年，坐父貶象州立山尉。

translations.literal: In Dazhong year 2, because of his father he was demoted to Lishan county lieutenant in Xiang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong 2, implicated in his father's fall, he was demoted to lieutenant of Lishan county in Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 二子幼，從父歿於崖州。

translations.literal: The two younger sons were small and followed their father to die at Yazhou.
translations.idiomatic: The two younger boys were still children; they followed their father to Yazhou and died there.

sentences.zh: 燁咸通初量移郴州郴縣尉，卒於桂陽。

translations.literal: Ye at the start of Xiantong was transferred by degree to Chen county lieutenant in Chenzhou and died at Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ye, early in Xiantong, was transferred to lieutenant of Chen county in Chenzhou and died at Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 子延古。

translations.literal: His son was Yangu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yangu.

sentences.zh: 【史評】史臣曰：臣總角時，亟聞耆德言衛公故事。

translations.literal: [Historian's appraisal] The historiographer says: When I was still a boy I often heard elders speak of Duke Wei's story.
translations.idiomatic: [Historian's appraisal] The historiographer writes: In my boyhood I often heard old men tell of Duke Wei's deeds.

sentences.zh: 是時天子神武，明於聽斷；

translations.literal: At that time the Son of Heaven was divinely martial and clear in hearing and deciding;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then was martial and keen of judgment;

sentences.zh: 公亦以身犯難，酬特達之遇。

translations.literal: the Duke also bore hardship in person, repaying exceptional favor.
translations.idiomatic: the Duke too risked himself in person, repaying singular trust.

sentences.zh: 言行計從，功成事遂，君臣之分，千載一時。

translations.literal: Word and deed followed plan; merit achieved, affairs concluded—the lord-and-minister division, a once-in-a-thousand-years moment.
translations.idiomatic: Counsel was heeded, campaigns succeeded—lord and minister in a bond that comes once in a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 觀其禁掖彌綸，巖廊啟奏，料敵制勝，襟靈獨斷，如由基命中，罔有虛發，實奇才也。

translations.literal: Observing his filling the inner palace with policy, opening memorials in the hall, calculating the enemy and controlling victory, his mind alone deciding—like Youji's hits, none wasted in the void—he was truly a rare talent.
translations.idiomatic: Watch him thread the inner court with policy, open debate in the hall, read the enemy and seize victory with a mind that answered to no one—like Yang Youji's arrows, none falling short: a genius of the age.

sentences.zh: 語文章，則嚴、馬扶輪；

translations.literal: Speaking of literature, Yan and Ma lend the wheel;
translations.idiomatic: In letters he stood where Yan Anguo and Sima Xiangru lend the wheel;

sentences.zh: 論政事，則蕭、曹避席。

translations.literal: discussing government, Xiao and Cao yield the mat.
translations.idiomatic: in statecraft Xiao He and Cao Shen would leave the mat.

sentences.zh: 罪其竊位，即太深文。

translations.literal: To condemn him for usurping place is over-strict wording.
translations.idiomatic: To charge him with seizing power is to press the indictment too far.

sentences.zh: 所可議者，不能釋憾解仇，以德報怨，泯是非於度外，齊彼我於環中。

translations.literal: What may be discussed is that he could not release resentment and dissolve enmity, repay injury with virtue, blur right and wrong beyond measure, and level self and other within the circle.
translations.idiomatic: What one may question is that he could not lay down old scores, repay injury with kindness, set aside the quarrel of right and wrong, or see foe and self as one within the round.

sentences.zh: 與夫市井之徒，力戰錐刀之末，淪身瘴海，可為傷心。

translations.literal: To struggle with marketplace men over the last sliver at the awl's point and sink his body in the malarial sea—this can move one to grief.
translations.idiomatic: That he fought market-town rivals over pennies and ended in the southern mists—there is heartbreak in that.

sentences.zh: 古所謂攫金都下，忽於市人，離婁不見於眉睫。

translations.literal: As the ancients said, snatching gold in the capital he forgets the crowd in the market; Li Lou does not see what lies on his eyelashes.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: a man who grabs gold beneath the capital forgets the crowd; Li Lou cannot see his own lashes.

sentences.zh: 才則才矣，語道則難。

translations.literal: Talented he was—but to speak of the Way is hard.
translations.idiomatic: A talent, yes—but the Way is another matter.

sentences.zh: 【贊】贊曰：公之智決，利若青萍。

translations.literal: [Appraisal] Appraisal says: The Duke's wisdom and decision, sharp as the Qingping blade.
translations.idiomatic: [Appraisal] The appraisal reads: His wit and resolve were keen as the Qingping sword.

sentences.zh: 破虜誅叛，摧枯建瓴。

translations.literal: Breaking barbarians and executing rebels, withering the dry and building the ridge-jar pour.
translations.idiomatic: He shattered barbarians and rebels, swept the withered and poured from the eaves—irresistible.

sentences.zh: 功成北闕，骨葬南溟。

translations.literal: Merit achieved at the northern gate, bones buried in the southern sea.
translations.idiomatic: Triumph at the northern palace; bones in the southern ocean.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼煙閣，誰上丹青？

translations.literal: Alas, the misty gallery—who will hang his portrait in colors?
translations.idiomatic: Alas for the Hall of Portraits in mist—who will brush him into the scroll?
